model.name: Airlines
model.description: Airlines is a global industry operating passenger and cargo flights across extensive route networks, offering premium travel experiences, loyalty programs, and hub-and-spoke connectivity linking cities worldwide.
model.core_business_processes: Flight Operations Management, Revenue Management and Pricing, Passenger Reservation and Ticketing, Crew Scheduling and Management, Aircraft Maintenance Repair and Overhaul (MRO), Cargo and Freight Management, Loyalty Program Administration, Ground Handling and Airport Operations, Route Network Planning and Scheduling, Regulatory Compliance and Safety Management

domains.name: flight
domains.description: Core flight operations data covering flight planning, dispatch releases, OOOI events (Out-Off-On-In gate times), block hours, fuel uplift, ACARS messaging, FMS data, operational control, flight schedules, actual departures and arrivals, delays, diversions, IROP handling, and real-time flight status. SSOT for all flight execution data. Aligns with Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops and Jeppesen Flight Planning System.

products.name: scheduled_flight
products.description: Master record for a planned flight operation as published in the airline's schedule. Represents the canonical scheduled flight leg with planned route, aircraft type, departure/arrival airports, scheduled times (STD/STA), flight number, codeshare indicators, operating carrier, service type (passenger/cargo/ferry), day-of-week frequency pattern, season validity (IATA summer/winter), and schedule status (active/suspended/cancelled). SSOT for all planned flight operations prior to day-of-operations. Each operated flight_leg references exactly one scheduled_flight as its planned baseline.
products.reference: IATA Schedule Reference Manual (SSIM)

attributes.name: arrival_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the scheduled arrival airport (e.g., LAX, CDG, SIN).

attributes.name: arrival_terminal
attributes.description: Scheduled arrival terminal identifier at the destination airport (e.g., Terminal 2, T5, Concourse A).

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned block time in minutes from gate departure (Out) to gate arrival (In). This is the scheduled elapsed time for the flight leg.

attributes.name: codeshare_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this scheduled flight is part of a codeshare agreement where multiple airlines market the same flight operation. True if codeshare, false if single-carrier operation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scheduled flight record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: day_of_week_pattern
attributes.description: Seven-character string indicating which days of the week the flight operates (1=operates, 0=does not operate). Position 1=Monday through position 7=Sunday (e.g., 1111100 = Monday-Friday only).
attributes.references: IATA SSIM Day of Week Encoding

attributes.name: departure_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the scheduled departure airport (e.g., JFK, LHR, DXB).

attributes.name: departure_terminal
attributes.description: Scheduled departure terminal identifier at the origin airport (e.g., Terminal 1, T3, Concourse B).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The first date this scheduled flight is valid and may operate. Start of the schedule validity period.

attributes.name: effective_until_date
attributes.description: The last date this scheduled flight is valid and may operate. End of the schedule validity period. Nullable for open-ended schedules.

attributes.name: etops_approval_indicator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Approval Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this scheduled flight route requires ETOPS certification for twin-engine aircraft operations over extended distances from diversion airports. True if ETOPS-certified route required.

attributes.name: flight_distance_km
attributes.description: Great circle distance between departure and arrival airports in kilometers. Used for RPK and ASK calculations.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scheduled flight record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: meal_service_code
attributes.description: Single-character IATA code indicating the type of meal service provided: B=Breakfast, L=Lunch, D=Dinner, S=Snack, M=Meal (unspecified), N=No meal service.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time in minutes required for passengers to make a legal connection from this flight to another flight at the arrival airport. Varies by airport, terminal, and connection type (domestic-domestic, domestic-international, international-international).

attributes.name: operating_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline code of the carrier actually operating the flight (e.g., AA for American Airlines, BA for British Airways).

attributes.name: published_date
attributes.description: Date when this scheduled flight was first published to Global Distribution Systems (GDS) and made available for booking. Critical for revenue management and distribution.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Status of regulatory approval from civil aviation authorities for this scheduled flight route and slot allocation: approved (fully authorized), pending (awaiting approval), conditional (approved with restrictions), or denied (not authorized).

attributes.name: route_network_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scheduled flight within the airlines route network strategy: hub_spoke (connecting through a hub), point_to_point (direct city-pair), regional_feeder (short-haul feed to hub), long_haul_international (intercontinental), or domestic_trunk (major domestic route).

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheduled flight: active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily not operating), cancelled (permanently removed), seasonal_inactive (out of season), or pending_approval (awaiting regulatory approval).

attributes.name: schedule_version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this schedule record. Incremented each time the scheduled flight details are modified (time changes, equipment changes, etc.). Supports schedule change tracking and audit.

attributes.name: scheduled_arrival_time
attributes.description: Published scheduled arrival time in local airport time. This is the planned gate arrival time (In time in OOOI).

attributes.name: scheduled_departure_time
attributes.description: Published scheduled departure time in local airport time. This is the planned gate departure time (Out time in OOOI).

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the flight service: passenger (revenue passenger service), cargo (freight-only), ferry (non-revenue repositioning), charter (non-scheduled charter), or positioning (crew/aircraft repositioning).

attributes.name: traffic_restriction_code
attributes.description: IATA traffic restriction code indicating any limitations on passenger or cargo carriage (e.g., C=Cargo only, G=Technical stop no traffic rights, F=Passenger service only). Empty if no restrictions.

attributes.name: wet_lease_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this scheduled flight is operated under a wet lease agreement (aircraft leased with crew, maintenance, and insurance from another carrier). True if wet lease operation.

products.name: flight_leg
products.description: Operational instance of a single flight leg actually operated or planned to be operated on a specific date. The atomic unit of flight execution and the central hub entity of the flight domain. Contains actual flight number, operating date, origin/destination airport pair, aircraft registration (tail number), cabin configuration, full flight status lifecycle with history (scheduled → boarding → departed → airborne → landed → arrived, or cancelled/diverted), status change timestamps with source attribution (ACARS, ATC feed, airport FIDS, manual OCC update), all OOOI timestamps (Out-Off-On-In), computed block hours and airborne time, estimated and actual departure/arrival times (ETD/ETA/ATD/ATA), gate/stand information, and public-facing status message. Links to scheduled_flight for planned baseline comparison. All operational flight records (dispatch, fuel, delays, performance) reference this entity. Supports real-time passenger notifications, airport FIDS integration, and OCC monitoring via NetLine/Ops.
products.reference: IATA SSIM / OOOI Event Standard

products.name: dispatch_release
products.description: Official dispatch release document authorizing a specific flight leg to depart. Contains dispatcher authorization, MEL (Minimum Equipment List) items accepted, fuel release quantities (planned uplift, minimum fuel, contingency, alternate, final reserve), alternate airports, NOTAM briefing package (relevant NOTAMs for departure/en-route/destination/alternate with operational significance flags), weather briefing package (METARs, TAFs, SIGMETs, PIREPs, winds-aloft for all relevant stations), ETOPS authorization if applicable, and dispatcher/captain sign-off timestamps. Mandatory regulatory document required by FAA 14 CFR Part 121.687 / EASA OPS for each commercial flight departure.
products.reference: FAA 14 CFR Part 121.593 / EASA OPS 1.1060

products.name: plan
products.description: Computerized flight plan for a specific flight leg, managed as a versioned document through its full lifecycle from initial filing to final crew-accepted Operational Flight Plan (OFP) loaded into the FMS. Contains route of flight (RNAV waypoints, airways, SIDs/STARs), planned altitude profile and step-climb schedule, estimated en-route time, fuel burn calculations by segment, alternate airports, wind and temperature data used, cost index, planned block hours, zero fuel weight, takeoff weight, landing weight, and performance data. Version status tracks progression: filed (submitted to ATC/ICAO), amended (re-cleared/updated), operational (final crew-accepted OFP loaded into FMS for execution). The operational version represents the definitive flight plan used by the crew and is the SSOT for planned route, fuel, and performance targets against which actuals are compared. Generated by Jeppesen Flight Planning System or equivalent.
products.reference: ICAO Doc 4444 PANS-ATM / ICAO Flight Plan Form

attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: alert_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.alert. Business justification: Dispatchers modify flight plans in response to active safety alerts (volcanic ash NOTAMs, airspace restriction alerts, manufacturer airworthiness bulletins). Linking flight_plan to the triggering safe

attributes.name: block_time_standard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.block_time_standard. Business justification: Flight dispatchers reference the authoritative block_time_standard when computing fuel requirements, crew duty time limits, and planned block hours in a flight plan. This is a direct regulatory and op

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.flight_leg. Business justification: Flight plans are operationally tied to specific flight legs (actual operations on a date), not just the schedule master. A flight plan is prepared for a specific operational instance. This FK links th

attributes.name: member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pilot-in-command who accepted and signed off on the operational flight plan.

attributes.name: scheduled_flight_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg for which this flight plan was generated.

attributes.name: alternate_airport_1_icao
attributes.description: Four-letter ICAO code of the primary alternate airport in case destination is unavailable.

attributes.name: alternate_airport_2_icao
attributes.description: Four-letter ICAO code of the secondary alternate airport.

attributes.name: alternate_fuel_kg
attributes.description: Fuel in kilograms required to fly from destination to the alternate airport and conduct an approach and landing.

attributes.name: arrival_airport_icao
attributes.description: Four-letter ICAO code of the destination airport.

attributes.name: contingency_fuel_kg
attributes.description: Contingency fuel in kilograms to account for unforeseen factors (typically 5% of trip fuel or 5 minutes holding fuel, whichever is greater).

attributes.name: cost_index
attributes.description: Cost index value used for flight planning optimization, balancing time cost versus fuel cost. Higher values favor speed; lower values favor fuel efficiency.
attributes.references: Boeing Flight Planning and Performance Manual

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flight plan record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cruise_altitude_ft
attributes.description: Planned cruise altitude in feet above mean sea level (MSL) for the primary cruise segment.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: cruise_speed_kts
attributes.description: Planned cruise speed in knots (true airspeed or indicated airspeed as per flight planning convention).

attributes.name: departure_airport_icao
attributes.description: Four-letter ICAO code of the departure airport.

attributes.name: etops_entry_point
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Entry Point
attributes.description: Waypoint or geographic coordinate where the flight enters ETOPS airspace.

attributes.name: etops_exit_point
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Exit Point
attributes.description: Waypoint or geographic coordinate where the flight exits ETOPS airspace.

attributes.name: etops_qualified_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Qualified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flight plan is qualified for ETOPS operations (extended-range twin-engine flights over water or remote areas).

attributes.name: filed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flight plan version was filed with Air Traffic Control (ATC) or ICAO Flight Plan Processing System.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: final_reserve_fuel_kg
attributes.description: Final reserve fuel in kilograms: minimum fuel required to fly for 30 minutes at holding speed at 1,500 feet above alternate airport elevation in standard conditions.

attributes.name: landing_weight_kg
attributes.description: Planned landing weight in kilograms at destination: takeoff weight minus trip fuel burn.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flight plan record was last updated.

attributes.name: operational_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flight plan version was accepted by the crew and loaded into the Flight Management System (FMS) as the operational flight plan (OFP).

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the flight plan. Filed: submitted to ATC/ICAO; Amended: re-cleared or updated; Operational: final crew-accepted OFP loaded into FMS for execution; Cancelled: plan withdrawn; Rejected: not accepted by ATC; Superseded: replaced by newer version.

attributes.name: planned_block_hours
attributes.description: Estimated total block time in hours from gate departure (Out) to gate arrival (In), including taxi, flight, and approach time.

attributes.name: planned_flight_time_hours
attributes.description: Estimated airborne time in hours from wheels-off to wheels-on.

attributes.name: planned_taxi_in_minutes
attributes.description: Estimated taxi time in minutes from landing to gate arrival.

attributes.name: planned_taxi_out_minutes
attributes.description: Estimated taxi time in minutes from gate departure to takeoff.

attributes.name: route_of_flight
attributes.description: Full textual representation of the planned route including RNAV waypoints, airways, Standard Instrument Departures (SIDs), and Standard Terminal Arrival Routes (STARs).

attributes.name: step_climb_schedule
attributes.description: Planned altitude step-climb profile showing waypoints and altitudes where the aircraft will request higher cruise levels to optimize fuel efficiency as weight decreases.

attributes.name: takeoff_weight_kg
attributes.description: Planned takeoff weight in kilograms: zero fuel weight plus total fuel on board at brake release.

attributes.name: total_fuel_required_kg
attributes.description: Total fuel required in kilograms: sum of trip fuel, contingency fuel, alternate fuel, final reserve fuel, taxi fuel, and any additional fuel.

attributes.name: trip_fuel_kg
attributes.description: Planned fuel burn in kilograms from takeoff to landing at destination airport.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this flight plan. Increments with each amendment or update to the plan for the same flight.

attributes.name: wind_data_source
attributes.description: Source of wind and temperature forecast data used in flight planning (e.g., NOAA GFS, ECMWF, proprietary meteorological service).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 3 - Meteorological Service for International Air Navigation

attributes.name: zero_fuel_weight_kg
attributes.description: Planned zero fuel weight in kilograms: aircraft operating empty weight plus payload (passengers, cargo, baggage) but excluding all usable fuel.

products.name: oooi_event
products.description: Captures the four key gate/runway timestamps for each flight leg: Out (pushback/gate departure), Off (wheels-off/takeoff), On (wheels-on/landing), and In (gate arrival/chocks-in). Each event record includes the event type, actual timestamp, source system (ACARS, manual entry, ADS-B), airport and runway/gate reference, and data quality flag. Foundation for block hours calculation, OTP (On-Time Performance) reporting, and DOT/IATA punctuality statistics.
products.reference: IATA OOOI Standard / ACARS ARINC 633

attributes.name: oooi_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each OOOI event record. Primary key for the OOOI event entity.

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg for which this OOOI event was recorded. Links to the operational flight leg in the flight operations domain.

attributes.name: acars_message_label
attributes.description: The ACARS message label identifier associated with this OOOI event transmission (e.g., H1 for OUT, 10 for OFF, 11 for ON, 12 for IN). Null if data source is not ACARS.

attributes.name: acars_message_number
attributes.description: The unique ACARS message sequence number for this OOOI event transmission. Used for message tracking and reconciliation. Null if data source is not ACARS.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: The tail number or registration identifier of the aircraft that generated this OOOI event. Used for cross-validation and aircraft-specific analysis.

attributes.name: airport_code
attributes.description: The three-letter IATA airport code where the OOOI event occurred (departure airport for OUT/OFF, arrival airport for ON/IN).

attributes.name: altitude_feet
attributes.description: The aircraft altitude in feet above mean sea level at the time of the OOOI event. Primarily populated for OFF and ON events from FMS or ADS-B data. Used for performance analysis.

attributes.name: correction_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description explaining why this OOOI event timestamp was corrected. Null if is_corrected is False. Used for audit trail and data quality improvement.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates the quality and reliability of the OOOI event data: VERIFIED (confirmed accurate), ESTIMATED (calculated or interpolated), CORRECTED (manually adjusted after initial capture), DISPUTED (conflicting data from multiple sources), PENDING (awaiting validation).

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: The system or method that captured and reported the OOOI event: ACARS (Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System), ADS-B (Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast), MANUAL (crew or ground staff entry), FMS (Flight Management System), OOOI_SENSOR (dedicated aircraft sensor), GROUND_SYSTEM (airport ground handling system).

attributes.name: delay_code
attributes.description: The IATA standard delay code indicating the reason for delay if the event was delayed (e.g., 11-Aircraft defects, 31-Flight deck crew, 81-Weather). Null if no delay occurred.

attributes.name: delay_minutes
attributes.description: The number of minutes this OOOI event occurred after the scheduled timestamp. Positive values indicate delay, negative values indicate early operation. Foundation for OTP and DOT delay reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Punctuality Standards, DOT 14 CFR Part 234

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the OOOI event occurred, recorded in UTC. This is the authoritative timestamp for the event used in OTP reporting and block hours calculation.

attributes.name: event_timestamp_local
attributes.description: The OOOI event timestamp converted to the local time zone of the airport where the event occurred. Used for operational reporting and crew scheduling.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: The type of OOOI event: OUT (pushback/gate departure), OFF (wheels-off/takeoff), ON (wheels-on/landing), IN (gate arrival/chocks-in). Foundation for block hours and OTP calculation.
attributes.references: IATA OOOI Standards, ACARS Messaging Standards

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: The commercial flight number associated with this OOOI event (e.g., AA100, DL2345). Used for operational tracking and passenger communication.

attributes.name: gate_stand
attributes.description: The gate or stand identifier where the OUT (pushback) or IN (arrival) event occurred. Null for OFF and ON events. Used for ground operations coordination.

attributes.name: ground_speed_knots
attributes.description: The aircraft ground speed in knots at the time of the OOOI event. Primarily populated for OFF and ON events. Used for performance and safety analysis.

attributes.name: is_corrected
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this OOOI event timestamp was manually corrected after initial capture due to data quality issues or system errors. True if corrected, False if original.

attributes.name: is_estimated
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this OOOI event timestamp was estimated or interpolated rather than directly captured from aircraft or ground systems. True if estimated, False if actual.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: The geographic latitude coordinate where the OOOI event occurred, captured from ADS-B or FMS. Primarily populated for OFF and ON events. Used for flight path analysis and safety investigations.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: The geographic longitude coordinate where the OOOI event occurred, captured from ADS-B or FMS. Primarily populated for OFF and ON events. Used for flight path analysis and safety investigations.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, comments, or additional context about this OOOI event. Used by flight operations staff to document unusual circumstances or data quality issues.

attributes.name: original_timestamp
attributes.description: The original OOOI event timestamp before any corrections were applied. Null if is_corrected is False. Preserved for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: otp_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this OOOI event is eligible for inclusion in OTP calculations per IATA or DOT standards. False if flight was cancelled, diverted, or otherwise excluded from OTP metrics.
attributes.references: IATA Punctuality Standards, DOT 14 CFR Part 234

attributes.name: processed_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the OOOI event data was validated, quality-checked, and integrated into the operational database. Used for data pipeline monitoring.

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the OOOI event data was received and recorded by the ground-based flight operations system. Used for data latency analysis and system performance monitoring.

attributes.name: reporting_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this OOOI event has been included in regulatory reporting submissions to DOT, IATA, or other authorities: REPORTED (included in submission), UNREPORTED (not yet submitted), EXCLUDED (intentionally omitted per reporting rules), AMENDED (corrected in a subsequent filing).
attributes.references: DOT 14 CFR Part 234, IATA Punctuality Standards

attributes.name: runway_identifier
attributes.description: The runway designation used for the OFF (takeoff) or ON (landing) event. Format follows ICAO runway naming conventions (e.g., 27L, 09R). Null for OUT and IN events.

attributes.name: scheduled_timestamp
attributes.description: The originally scheduled timestamp for this OOOI event type (scheduled departure for OUT, scheduled takeoff for OFF, scheduled landing for ON, scheduled arrival for IN). Used to calculate delay and OTP metrics.

products.name: fuel_uplift
products.description: Records actual fuel loaded onto an aircraft for a specific flight leg at a specific station. Contains fuel quantity uplift (kg/lbs and litres), fuel density, fuel type (Jet-A, Jet-A1, JP-8), fuelling company, into-plane agent, fuel ticket number, fuel price per unit, total fuel cost, pre-fuelling quantity on board, post-fuelling quantity on board, and fuelling timestamp. Critical for fuel cost accounting, fuel efficiency analysis, and CORSIA carbon reporting.
products.reference: IATA Fuel Cost Management / CORSIA MRV

attributes.name: fuel_uplift_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fuel uplift transaction record.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Fuel supplier invoices flow through AP for payment processing and three-way matching (uplift record, invoice, payment). Links operational fuel transaction to financial settlement for cash management,

attributes.name: dispatch_release_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.dispatch_release. Business justification: The dispatch release contains the planned_fuel_uplift_kg authorized for the flight. The fuel_uplift record captures what was actually loaded. Linking fuel_uplift directly to dispatch_release enables f

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg for which fuel was uplifted.

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Fuel uplift occurs at specific stations; linking enables fuel cost allocation by station, vendor performance tracking, price variance analysis, and station-level fuel consumption reporting. Core finan

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: The tail number or registration code of the aircraft that received the fuel uplift.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: carbon_emission_kg
attributes.description: Estimated carbon dioxide emissions in kilograms resulting from the combustion of the uplifted fuel, used for CORSIA reporting.
attributes.references: ICAO CORSIA - Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel uplift record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: fuel_batch_number
attributes.description: Batch or lot number of the fuel supplied, used for quality traceability.

attributes.name: fuel_density
attributes.description: Density of the fuel at the time of uplift, measured in kilograms per litre, used for mass-volume conversions.
attributes.references: ASTM D4052 - Density and Relative Density of Liquids

attributes.name: fuel_price_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the fuel price.

attributes.name: fuel_price_per_unit
attributes.description: Price per unit (per kilogram or per litre) of fuel charged by the supplier.

attributes.name: fuel_quality_certificate_number
attributes.description: Certificate number issued by the fuel supplier confirming fuel quality and compliance with aviation standards.

attributes.name: fuel_quantity_kg
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel uplifted measured in kilograms.

attributes.name: fuel_quantity_lbs
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel uplifted measured in pounds.

attributes.name: fuel_quantity_litres
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel uplifted measured in litres.

attributes.name: fuel_surcharge_amount
attributes.description: Additional surcharge or fee applied to the fuel uplift transaction.

attributes.name: fuel_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Temperature of the fuel at the time of uplift, measured in degrees Celsius, used for density correction.

attributes.name: fuel_ticket_number
attributes.description: Unique ticket or document number issued by the fueling company for this uplift transaction.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of aviation fuel uplifted (e.g., Jet-A, Jet-A1, JP-8).

attributes.name: fuel_uplift_status
attributes.description: Current status of the fuel uplift transaction (e.g., completed, partial, cancelled, disputed).

attributes.name: fueling_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of the fueling operation in minutes.

attributes.name: fueling_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the fuel uplift operation began.

attributes.name: fueling_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the fuel uplift operation was completed, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: into_plane_agent
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the into-plane agent or ground handler responsible for the physical fueling operation.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: Invoice number issued by the fuel supplier for this uplift transaction.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: Method of payment used for the fuel uplift (e.g., credit account, cash, card, prepaid).

attributes.name: post_fueling_quantity_kg
attributes.description: Total quantity of fuel on board the aircraft after the uplift, measured in kilograms.

attributes.name: pre_fueling_quantity_kg
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel already on board the aircraft before the uplift, measured in kilograms.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes or comments related to the fuel uplift transaction.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Tax amount applied to the fuel uplift transaction, including excise or environmental taxes.

attributes.name: total_fuel_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of the fuel uplift transaction in the specified currency.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel uplift record was last updated in the system.

products.name: delay_record
products.description: Captures delay events associated with a flight leg including primary and secondary IATA delay codes (AHM 730 standard), delay duration in minutes, responsible department/station, delay description narrative, delay category (airline, ATC, airport, weather, pax-related), and whether the delay was reactionary (caused by late inbound aircraft). Supports OTP reporting, DOT delay reporting, root cause analysis, and operational performance management.
products.reference: IATA AHM 730 Delay Codes Standard

attributes.name: delay_record_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the delay record. Primary key.

attributes.name: absence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.absence. Business justification: Crew absence (sick call, no-show) is a primary IATA delay code category. DOT on-time reporting and delay cost attribution require linking a delay record directly to the crew absence that caused it. de

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: EU261/DOT delay compensation payments are processed as AP transactions. The delay_record has compensation_issued_flag and delay_cost_estimate_usd. Airlines pay compensation via AP to passengers or han

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Delay costs (crew overtime, passenger compensation, missed slot fees, reactionary delays) are allocated to responsible cost centres for operational cost analysis, CASK calculation, and departmental pe

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg that experienced this delay.

attributes.name: irop_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.flight_irop_event. Business justification: A delay record is frequently triggered by or associated with an IROP event (e.g., weather system, ATC ground stop, aircraft swap). Adding flight_irop_event_id to delay_record allows grouping all delay

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Safety occurrences (bird strikes, medical emergencies, security events) directly cause operational delays. Delay analysis and regulatory reporting (DOT 14 CFR Part 234) require linking delay records t

attributes.name: responsible_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Delay accountability requires linking to responsible station entity for performance tracking, cost allocation of controllable delays, station manager accountability, and regulatory DOT reporting by st

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Maintenance-caused delays must reference the specific work order driving the delay. Required for IATA delay code reporting (ATA/ATM codes), reliability program analysis, and maintenance delay cost att

attributes.name: affected_passenger_count
attributes.description: Number of passengers (Pax) affected by this delay event. Used for customer impact assessment and compensation calculations.

attributes.name: compensation_issued_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether passenger compensation (monetary or vouchers) was issued as a result of this delay under EU261, DOT, or airline policy. True if compensation issued, False if not.

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of corrective or preventive actions taken to resolve the delay or prevent recurrence. Used for continuous improvement and safety management system (SMS) tracking.
attributes.references: ICAO SMS Framework, Internal Quality Management

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system from which this delay record originated (e.g., Lufthansa Systems NetLine/Ops, Jeppesen Flight Planning, manual entry by operations staff, ACARS messaging, or other systems).

attributes.name: delay_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the delay cause: airline operational issues, ATC (Air Traffic Control) restrictions, airport facility problems, weather conditions, passenger-related issues, reactionary delays from late inbound aircraft, security events, or other causes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: airline_operational|air_traffic_control|airport_facilities|weather|passenger_related|reactionary|security|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: delay_cost_estimate_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Delay Cost Estimate in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated financial cost of the delay in US dollars, including crew overtime, passenger compensation, fuel burn, missed connections, and operational disruption. Used for cost-benefit analysis and delay reduction initiatives.

attributes.name: delay_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description providing detailed context and explanation of the delay event, root cause, and any corrective actions taken.

attributes.name: delay_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the delay event measured in minutes. Used for OTP (On-Time Performance) calculations and DOT reporting.

attributes.name: delay_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the resolution or end of the delay event in UTC. Nullable if delay is ongoing or not yet resolved.

attributes.name: delay_notification_sent_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when delay notification was sent to passengers via SMS, email, or mobile app. Used to measure compliance with customer communication standards.

attributes.name: delay_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of multiple delay events for the same flight leg. Allows tracking of multiple delay causes on a single flight.

attributes.name: delay_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the beginning of the delay event in UTC. Used to calculate delay duration and analyze delay patterns by time of day.

attributes.name: delay_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the delay record: open (delay ongoing), resolved (delay ended), under investigation (root cause analysis in progress), closed (finalized and archived), or disputed (under review or challenge).

attributes.name: delay_verification_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the delay record was verified and approved by a supervisor. Nullable if verification is pending.

attributes.name: is_controllable_delay
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the delay was within the airline's control (e.g., maintenance, crew scheduling) versus external factors (e.g., weather, ATC). Used for internal performance accountability and root cause analysis.

attributes.name: is_reactionary_delay
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this delay was reactionary (caused by a late inbound aircraft from a previous flight leg). True if reactionary, False if not.

attributes.name: is_reportable_to_dot
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this delay must be reported to the US Department of Transportation under 14 CFR Part 234 (applies to delays of 15 minutes or more for covered carriers). True if reportable, False if not.

attributes.name: missed_connection_count
attributes.description: Number of passengers who missed their connecting flights as a result of this delay. Used for IROP (Irregular Operations) management and customer service planning.

attributes.name: primary_delay_code
attributes.description: Two-digit IATA delay code representing the primary cause of the delay per AHM 730 standard (e.g., 11=Aircraft defects, 31=Flight deck crew, 81=Weather).

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this delay record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this delay record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: responsible_department_code
attributes.description: Internal department code identifying the organizational unit responsible for or associated with the delay (e.g., MX=Maintenance, OPS=Operations, CREW=Crew Scheduling, GND=Ground Handling).

products.name: diversion
products.description: Records flight diversions where an aircraft lands at an airport other than the planned destination. Contains diversion reason (weather, medical, mechanical, ATC, security), diversion airport, time of diversion decision, actual landing time at diversion airport, subsequent disposition (continued to destination, returned to origin, cancelled), passenger handling actions taken, and estimated cost impact. Supports IROP management, regulatory reporting, and passenger care obligations.
products.reference: IATA IROP Management Guidelines / DOT Reporting

attributes.name: diversion_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the flight diversion event. Primary key.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Diversions trigger immediate AP payments for hotel_accommodation, meal_vouchers, and ground transport (flags present on diversion). Airlines process these as AP invoices from hotels/caterers; linking

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Diversions incur incremental costs (extra fuel, ground handling, passenger accommodation, crew expenses) that must be allocated to specific cost centres for operational variance analysis, budget contr

attributes.name: dispatch_release_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.dispatch_release. Business justification: When a diversion occurs, a new or amended dispatch release must be issued for the continuation flight from the diversion airport. diversion already has dispatch_release_updated_flag (boolean) indicati

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the flight that was diverted. Links to the flight operations record.

attributes.name: irop_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.flight_irop_event. Business justification: A diversion is a key outcome of an IROP event. Multiple diversions can be caused by the same IROP event (e.g., a severe weather system forcing several aircraft to divert). Adding flight_irop_event_id

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Diversions are significant safety events requiring occurrence reporting under ICAO Annex 13 and national regulations. Direct linkage enables Safety Management System to track diversion→occurrence rela

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Diversion events require station entity link for ground handler coordination, passenger care resource allocation, diversion cost tracking by station, hotel/meal vendor management, and station capabili

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Technical diversions generate work orders at the diversion station. Linking diversion.work_order_id → maintenance.work_order.work_order_id enables technical diversion root cause analysis, cost attribu

attributes.name: actual_gate_arrival_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Gate Arrival Timestamp at Diversion Airport
attributes.description: Date and time when the aircraft arrived at the gate at the diversion airport. Completes the In event of OOOI tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: actual_landing_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Landing Timestamp at Diversion Airport
attributes.description: Date and time when the aircraft touched down at the diversion airport. Part of OOOI (Out-Off-On-In) event tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: Tail number or registration mark of the aircraft that was diverted. Used for aircraft-specific tracking and maintenance correlation.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: airport_icao_code
attributes.description: Four-letter ICAO airport code of the diversion airport. Provides international standard identifier for flight planning and ATC coordination.

attributes.name: atc_coordination_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier provided by Air Traffic Control (ATC) for the diversion coordination. Used for operational tracking and incident investigation.

attributes.name: compensation_eligibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers are eligible for monetary compensation under applicable passenger rights regulations due to the diversion. True if eligible; False otherwise.
attributes.references: EU Regulation 261/2004, DOT Consumer Protection Rules

attributes.name: continuation_departure_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the continuation flight departed from the diversion airport toward the original destination. Null if no continuation occurred. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: continuation_flight_number
attributes.description: Flight number assigned to the continuation flight if the aircraft or passengers continued to the original destination after the diversion. Null if flight was cancelled or returned to origin.

attributes.name: cost_impact_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated cost impact amount.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this diversion record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: crew_duty_time_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the diversion caused crew duty time or flight time limitations to be exceeded or approached, requiring crew replacement or schedule adjustments. True if impacted; False otherwise.
attributes.references: FAA 14 CFR Part 117 - Flight and Duty Limitations

attributes.name: decision_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the decision to divert was made by the pilot-in-command or operational control. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: dispatch_release_updated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a new or amended dispatch release was issued for the continuation flight from the diversion airport. True if updated; False otherwise.

attributes.name: disposition_action
attributes.description: Subsequent operational action taken after landing at the diversion airport. Continued_to_destination indicates flight resumed to original destination; returned_to_origin indicates flight returned to departure airport; cancelled indicates flight was terminated; aircraft_swap indicates passengers transferred to another aircraft; overnight_recovery indicates passengers accommodated overnight.

attributes.name: diversion_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the diversion event, used for operational tracking and reporting. Format: DIV followed by numeric sequence.

attributes.name: diversion_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the diversion event. Tracks progression from initial declaration through resolution.

attributes.name: estimated_cost_impact_amount
attributes.description: Estimated total financial cost impact of the diversion event, including fuel, landing fees, passenger care, crew expenses, and operational disruption costs. Expressed in the airline's reporting currency.

attributes.name: fuel_uplift_at_diversion_kg
attributes.description: Amount of fuel uplifted at the diversion airport in kilograms. Required if the aircraft continued to the original destination or another airport after the diversion.

attributes.name: ground_time_duration_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Ground Time Duration at Diversion Airport (Minutes)
attributes.description: Total time in minutes that the aircraft spent on the ground at the diversion airport, from gate arrival to departure (if continuation occurred) or final shutdown.

attributes.name: hotel_accommodation_provided_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether hotel accommodation was provided to passengers due to the diversion. True if accommodation was arranged; False otherwise.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this diversion record was last updated in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: meal_voucher_provided_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether meal vouchers or meals were provided to passengers due to the diversion. True if meals were provided; False otherwise.

attributes.name: notam_reference
attributes.description: Reference to any relevant NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) that contributed to or was issued in relation to the diversion event.

attributes.name: passenger_care_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of passenger care actions provided at the diversion airport, including meals, accommodation, rebooking, ground transportation, and communication. Documents compliance with passenger rights regulations.

attributes.name: passenger_count_diverted
attributes.description: Total number of passengers (Pax) on board the aircraft at the time of diversion. Used for passenger care planning and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: planned_destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code of the original planned destination airport before diversion was declared.

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Primary reason category for the diversion. Weather includes wx conditions at destination; medical includes passenger or crew medical emergencies; mechanical includes aircraft technical issues; fuel includes fuel shortage or fuel planning issues; ATC includes air traffic control restrictions; security includes security threats or incidents; airport_closure includes runway closures or airport operational issues. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: weather|medical|mechanical|fuel|atc|security|airport_closure — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative explanation of the specific circumstances that led to the diversion decision. Provides operational context beyond the reason code.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 13 - Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation

attributes.name: regulatory_report_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the diversion event requires formal reporting to aviation regulatory authorities (FAA, EASA, national CAA). True if reporting is required; False otherwise.

attributes.name: regulatory_report_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the required regulatory report was submitted to the aviation authority. Null if no report was required or not yet submitted. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: safety_report_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of any safety report filed in the airline's Safety Management System (SMS) related to the diversion event. Used for safety trend analysis and continuous improvement.

attributes.name: weather_condition_description
attributes.description: Description of the weather (wx) conditions at the planned destination or en route that contributed to the diversion decision, if weather was a factor. Includes visibility, ceiling, wind, precipitation, and other meteorological phenomena.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 3 - Meteorological Service for International Air Navigation

products.name: irop_event
products.description: Irregular Operations (IROP) event master record capturing disruptions that affect multiple flights or require operational recovery actions. Covers event type (weather, ATC ground stop, airport closure, aircraft AOG, crew shortage, security), affected station(s), event start/end times, severity level, CDM (Collaborative Decision Making) session reference, recovery plan status, and estimated total delay minutes and passengers affected. Distinct from individual delay_record or diversion — represents the root cause event driving multiple disruptions.
products.reference: IATA IROP Management / FAA CDM Program

attributes.name: irop_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the irregular operations event record. Primary key for the flight IROP event entity.

attributes.name: affected_station_id
