attributes.description: Aggregate of all government taxes, airport fees, and surcharges (e.g., PFC, September 11th Security Fee, fuel surcharge YQ/YR) applied to the ticket. Part of the MONETARY_TRIPLET adjustment component. Detailed tax breakdown is stored at coupon level.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; DOT 14 CFR Part 382; FAA PFC Program; IATA TACT Rules

attributes.name: ticket_number
attributes.description: The globally unique 13-digit IATA-format ticket number comprising the 3-digit airline numeric code, a 10-digit serial number, and a check digit. This is the primary external business identifier for the issued e-ticket, used in BSP/ARC settlement, GDS lookups, and passenger check-in. BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: ticket_status
attributes.description: Current state of the e-ticket in its lifecycle. 'open' = issued and valid for travel; 'used' = all coupons flown; 'refunded' = fare returned to passenger; 'voided' = cancelled within BSP/ARC void window; 'exchanged' = reissued against a new ticket; 'lifted' = coupon checked in and boarded. LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; DOT 14 CFR Part 250

attributes.name: total_fare_amount
attributes.description: Total amount charged to the passenger including base fare, taxes, and all fees. Equals base_fare_amount + tax_total_amount. MONETARY_TRIPLET net total. Used for BSP/ARC settlement, revenue recognition, and passenger receipt.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; DOT Form 41

attributes.name: tour_code
attributes.description: Alphanumeric tour code printed on the ticket, used to identify negotiated/net fares, bulk fares, or tour operator contracts. Required for BSP/ARC net remit reporting and commission audit. Blank for published fares.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; IATA BSP Manual

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ticket record in the lakehouse silver layer, capturing status changes, reissues, or corrections. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.

attributes.name: void_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the ticket was voided within the BSP/ARC void window (typically same-day or T+1). Null for non-voided tickets. Required for BSP/ARC void transaction reporting and revenue reversal in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; IATA Resolution 722

products.name: ticket_coupon
products.description: Individual flight coupon record within an e-ticket, representing one segment of travel. Each e-ticket may contain up to four flight coupons. Captures coupon number, flight number, origin and destination, departure date, cabin class, booking class (RBD), fare basis code, not-valid-before/after dates, baggage allowance, coupon status (open/used/lifted/flown/refunded/voided/suspended/exchanged), stopover indicator, and actual flight date used. SSOT for coupon-level revenue recognition and BSP/ARC coupon reporting.
products.reference: IATA Resolution 722 Flight Coupon / BSP Coupon Record

attributes.name: ticket_coupon_id
attributes.description: Primary key for ticket_coupon

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft. Business justification: Ticket coupons represent flown segments; airlines must track which aircraft operated each coupon for revenue allocation to specific assets, aircraft-level RASK/CASK analysis, and lease cost recovery c

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.cabin_configuration. Business justification: Revenue integrity and passenger experience audits require knowing which cabin configuration was actually in service when a coupon was lifted. Equipment swaps change the delivered product; this link su

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Each coupon represents revenue recognized by a specific legal entity. Required for consolidated financial statements and intercompany eliminations in multi-entity airline operations.

attributes.name: fare_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.fare_class. Business justification: Each coupon has a booking_class attribute (RBD code). This should reference the authoritative fare_class master which defines the RBD hierarchy and yield management rules. Standard N:1 relationship. N

attributes.name: fare_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.fare. Business justification: Each flight coupon within a ticket can have its own fare basis (especially for multi-segment journeys with different fare components). The fare_basis_code in ticket_coupon should reference the authori

attributes.name: flight_inventory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.flight_inventory. Business justification: Each ticket coupon is issued against a specific flight inventory allocation, consuming a seat from the booking class bucket. Critical for inventory deduction, lift reporting, and reconciling sold vs.

attributes.name: flight_number_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.flight_number. Business justification: Ticket coupons are issued against specific scheduled flight numbers for revenue accounting, OTP-revenue correlation analysis, and IATA BSP settlement. The existing flight_number plain text column is a

attributes.name: inventory_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.inventory_leg. Business justification: Revenue accounting reconciles ticket coupons against inventory legs for load factor reporting and leg-based revenue proration. ticket_coupon links to flight.flight_leg but not to inventory_leg — the i

attributes.name: marketing_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: Codeshare revenue accounting requires distinguishing the marketing carrier (sells the seat) from the operating carrier. Marketing carrier revenue share calculations and GDS distribution reporting depe

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Ticket coupons require origin station linkage for revenue accounting, interline settlement proration, station P&L reporting, and BSP/ARC reconciliation. Origin_airport_code is denormalized station ref

attributes.name: pax_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the passenger record associated with this coupon, enabling coupon-level revenue attribution to an individual traveller.

attributes.name: pnr_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Passenger Name Record (PNR) associated with this coupon, linking the coupon to the originating reservation in the Amadeus Altéa Passenger Service System (PSS).

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Each coupon represents a flight segment on a specific route; essential for revenue allocation, prorate calculations between carriers, interline settlement, and route-level revenue performance analysis

attributes.name: technical_log_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.technical_log. Business justification: Each ticket coupon represents a flown sector; the technical log records airworthiness state for that exact sector. Aviation operations link coupon-level flight data to the technical log for AOG impact

attributes.name: ticket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent e-ticket record to which this coupon belongs. Each e-ticket may contain up to four flight coupons (one per segment).

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Airlines track which maintenance work orders caused flight disruptions affecting specific ticket coupons for passenger compensation claims, revenue impact analysis, and operational performance reporti

attributes.name: actual_departure_date
attributes.description: Actual calendar date on which the passenger departed on this coupon segment. May differ from scheduled departure date due to IROP (Irregular Operations), reprotection, or voluntary rebooking. Used for revenue recognition and OTP reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; DOT On-Time Performance Reporting

attributes.name: baggage_allowance
attributes.description: Free checked baggage allowance associated with this coupon, expressed either as piece concept (e.g., 2PC) or weight concept (e.g., 23KG) per IATA Resolution 302. Drives ancillary revenue opportunity identification and customer service.

attributes.name: booking_class
attributes.description: Single-letter Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) representing the fare class inventory bucket in which the seat was booked (e.g., Y, B, M, Q, V). Drives yield management, load factor analysis, and revenue accounting. Aligns with Sabre AirVision inventory buckets.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

attributes.name: cabin_class
attributes.description: IATA cabin class code indicating the physical cabin in which the passenger travels: F=First, C=Business, W=Premium Economy, Y=Economy. Drives revenue segmentation, RASK analysis, and yield reporting.

attributes.name: coupon_number
attributes.description: Sequential coupon number within the e-ticket (1 through 4), indicating the position of this flight segment in the itinerary. IATA mandates a maximum of four coupons per ticket.

attributes.name: coupon_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the flight coupon per IATA coupon status codes: O=Open for use, A=Airport control (lifted), F=Flown/used, R=Refunded, V=Voided, S=Suspended, E=Exchanged, L=Lifted/boarded. SSOT for coupon-level revenue recognition and BSP/ARC coupon reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: O|A|F|R|V|S|E|L — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; BSP Manual for Agents

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which this coupon record was first created in the source Passenger Service System (Amadeus Altéa). Used for audit trail and data lineage in the silver layer.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; Amadeus Altéa PSS; ISO 8601

attributes.name: departure_date
attributes.description: Scheduled calendar date of departure for this coupon segment as printed on the ticket (yyyy-MM-dd). Used for validity checking, revenue period allocation, and BSP/ARC settlement date matching.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: IATA 3-letter airport code for the arrival point of this coupon segment (e.g., CDG, SIN). Used for route-level revenue analysis and O&D (origin-destination) yield management.

attributes.name: exchange_ticket_number
attributes.description: 13-digit ticket number of the original e-ticket that was exchanged to produce this coupon. Populated when coupon_status is E (Exchanged). Required for BSP/ARC exchange transaction reporting and revenue accounting audit trail.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: fare_amount
attributes.description: Base fare amount allocated to this individual coupon segment in the ticket currency, before taxes and surcharges. Used for coupon-level revenue recognition, BSP/ARC settlement, and yield (revenue per RPK) calculation.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; IFRS 15 (Revenue Recognition)

attributes.name: fare_basis_code
attributes.description: Alphanumeric code (up to 15 characters) identifying the specific fare rule set applied to this coupon, encoding cabin, booking class, seasonality, advance purchase, and restrictions (e.g., YLOWUS, QAPEX14). SSOT for fare rule application and revenue accounting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ATPCO Fare Filing Standards

attributes.name: fare_construction_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates the fare construction method applied to this coupon: NUC=Neutral Unit of Construction (IATA proration), SITI=Sold Inside/Ticketed Inside, SOTO=Sold Outside/Ticketed Outside, SITO=Sold Inside/Ticketed Outside, SOTI=Sold Outside/Ticketed Inside. Governs BSP settlement currency conversion rules.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; IATA Fare Construction Rules; BSP Manual

attributes.name: fare_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 3-letter currency code in which the fare amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for BSP/ARC settlement and multi-currency revenue reporting.

attributes.name: flown_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the passenger actually flew this coupon segment, as recorded by the departure control system at boarding. Populated when coupon_status is F (Flown). Triggers revenue recognition under IFRS 15.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; IFRS 15 (Revenue Recognition); Amadeus Altéa DCS

attributes.name: issuing_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the e-ticket containing this coupon was issued. Used for revenue period allocation, BSP/ARC reporting cycles, and advance purchase restriction validation.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which this coupon record was most recently modified in the source system. Tracks status changes, exchanges, refunds, and reprotection events for audit and incremental load processing.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; Amadeus Altéa PSS; ISO 8601

attributes.name: lifted_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the coupon was lifted (scanned/validated) at the boarding gate. Captured by the Amadeus Altéa Departure Control System (DCS). Used for OOOI event correlation and OTP measurement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; Amadeus Altéa DCS; ICAO Annex 6

attributes.name: not_valid_after_date
attributes.description: Latest date on which this coupon may be used for travel, as specified by the fare rule. Enforced at check-in and boarding. Null indicates no upper validity restriction (open-dated coupon).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ATPCO Fare Filing Standards

attributes.name: not_valid_before_date
attributes.description: Earliest date on which this coupon may be used for travel, as specified by the fare rule. Enforced at check-in and boarding. Null indicates no lower validity restriction.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ATPCO Fare Filing Standards

attributes.name: nuc_amount
attributes.description: Fare amount expressed in IATA Neutral Units of Construction (NUC), the currency-neutral unit used for international fare proration and interline revenue accounting. Converted to local currency using IATA Rate of Exchange (ROE).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; IATA Fare Construction Rules; BSP Manual

attributes.name: operating_carrier_code
attributes.description: IATA 2-character designator of the airline actually operating the flight. Differs from the marketing carrier code in codeshare and interline arrangements. Required for BSP/ARC settlement and DOT reporting.

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: Amount refunded for this coupon when coupon_status is R (Refunded), net of applicable cancellation penalties. Used for revenue reversal accounting, BSP/ARC refund settlement, and customer refund tracking.

attributes.name: refund_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the refund for this coupon was processed. Populated when coupon_status is R (Refunded). Used for revenue reversal period allocation and BSP/ARC refund cycle reporting.

attributes.name: settlement_type
attributes.description: Identifies the settlement channel through which this coupon will be or has been financially settled: BSP=IATA Billing and Settlement Plan, ARC=Airlines Reporting Corporation (US domestic), DIRECT=direct airline settlement, INTERLINE=interline billing via IATA Clearing House.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: stopover_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this coupon point constitutes a stopover (True) or a connection (False) per IATA fare construction rules. A stopover is a deliberate break in journey exceeding 24 hours domestically or 24 hours internationally. Affects fare construction and through-fare applicability.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; IATA Fare Construction Rules

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total taxes, fees, and surcharges (YQ/YR fuel surcharge, airport taxes, PFC, government levies) allocated to this coupon segment. Required for BSP/ARC settlement and regulatory tax remittance reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; DOT 14 CFR Part 399; PFC regulations (49 U.S.C. 40117)

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: Total amount for this coupon segment (fare_amount + tax_amount) in the ticket currency. Used as the gross revenue figure for coupon-level BSP/ARC settlement and revenue accounting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; IFRS 15

attributes.name: void_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which this coupon was voided. Populated when coupon_status is V (Voided). Voiding is only permitted on the date of issuance per BSP/ARC rules. Used for revenue accounting and settlement reconciliation.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

products.name: revenue_emd
products.description: Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) record for ancillary services sold in conjunction with or independently of an air ticket. Captures EMD number, EMD type (EMD-A associated / EMD-S standalone), service type code (IATA RFIC/RFISC), service description (excess baggage, seat upgrade, lounge access, priority boarding, etc.), associated ticket number, coupon reference, amount, currency, form of payment, issue date, issuing office, EMD status (open/used/refunded/voided), and BSP/ARC reporting flag. SSOT for ancillary revenue document lifecycle.
products.reference: IATA Resolution 787 (EMD) / IATA RFIC/RFISC Standard

attributes.name: revenue_emd_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: bsp_settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.bsp_settlement. Business justification: revenue_emd (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) records ancillary services that are settled through BSP/ARC just like tickets. Currently revenue_emd stores bsp_arc_billing_period (STRING) and bsp_arc_

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: EMDs (ancillary revenue) are issued by legal entities and must be attributed for IFRS 15 revenue recognition and financial reporting by legal entity.

attributes.name: ffp_member_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to loyalty.ffp_member. Business justification: Ancillary purchases (baggage, seats, lounge) earn loyalty miles. EMDs must link to FFP member for accrual posting and tier benefit validation. Replaces denormalized frequent_flyer_number with proper F

attributes.name: flight_inventory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.flight_inventory. Business justification: EMDs for ancillary services (seat upgrades, excess baggage, lounge access) are tied to specific flights. Per-flight ancillary revenue reporting and EMD reconciliation require flight_inventory_id. reve

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.flight_leg. Business justification: EMDs for flight-specific ancillary services (seat upgrades, excess baggage, priority boarding on a specific leg) must be reconciled against the operated flight_leg for ancillary revenue per-flight P&L

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: EMD ancillary revenue must be posted to the GL for IFRS 15 ancillary revenue recognition reporting. Airlines track EMD revenue (seat upgrades, baggage fees) as a distinct GL line. No existing FK cover

attributes.name: issuing_crew_member_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.crew_member. Business justification: Tracks cabin crew member who sold ancillary service onboard (baggage upgrade, seat selection, meals). Essential for onboard revenue attribution, crew sales incentive programs, and commission calculati

attributes.name: itinerary_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservation.itinerary_segment. Business justification: EMDs for segment-specific ancillaries (seat upgrades, excess baggage on a specific leg) must reference the itinerary segment. Segment-level ancillary revenue reporting and EMD coupon reconciliation re

attributes.name: pnr_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservation.pnr. Business justification: EMDs are issued against PNRs for ancillary services. Linking revenue_emd to pnr enables ancillary revenue tracking per booking, EMD reconciliation, and IATA resolution manual compliance. revenue_emd.p

attributes.name: pricing_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.pricing_record. Business justification: EMDs (Electronic Miscellaneous Documents) for ancillary services may be priced through the same pricing engine as tickets. Linking EMD to the pricing_record that calculated its cost establishes the pr

attributes.name: product_catalog_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ancillary.product_catalog. Business justification: Revenue EMDs represent sold ancillary services. Linking to the ancillary product catalog enables revenue-by-product reporting, IFRS 15 performance obligation identification, and ancillary revenue acco

attributes.name: ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.ticket. Business justification: EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) is issued in conjunction with or independently of a ticket. The emd table has associated_ticket_number (STRING) which is a business key reference. Adding ticket

attributes.name: base_amount
attributes.description: The base fare component of the EMD before taxes and fees, in the transaction currency. Used for yield analysis, RASK computation, and ancillary revenue decomposition in Sabre AirVision Revenue Management.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Ticketing Handbook; Sabre AirVision

attributes.name: coupon_number
attributes.description: Sequential coupon number within the EMD document (1–4), identifying the specific service coupon. Each coupon corresponds to one service event or flight segment. Used for coupon-level status tracking and BSP/ARC settlement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this EMD record was first captured in the lakehouse silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and SLA monitoring of data pipeline latency.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction currency in which the EMD was issued (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency BSP/ARC settlement and SAP S/4HANA FX revaluation.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code of the destination station for the associated flight segment (e.g., LAX, CDG). Used for route-level ancillary revenue analytics and geographic revenue attribution.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Airport Coding Directory

attributes.name: emd_number
attributes.description: The 13-digit IATA-standard EMD document number, structured as airline code (3 digits) + form code (1 digit) + serial number (6 digits) + check digit (1 digit) + coupon count (2 digits). This is the externally-known business identifier used in BSP/ARC settlement and passenger-facing communications.

attributes.name: emd_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the EMD coupon: open (issued, not yet used), used (service delivered), refunded (amount returned to passenger), voided (cancelled same-day before BSP/ARC lift), exchanged (reissued as new EMD), suspended (temporarily held). Drives revenue recognition and BSP/ARC settlement eligibility. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|used|refunded|voided|exchanged|suspended — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Ticketing Handbook; Sabre AirVision

attributes.name: emd_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the EMD is an EMD-A (Associated — linked to an air ticket coupon) or EMD-S (Standalone — issued independently of a ticket, e.g., lounge access, excess baggage sold separately). Drives BSP/ARC settlement routing and revenue accounting treatment.

attributes.name: equivalent_amount
attributes.description: Total EMD amount converted to the airline's base/reporting currency using the IATA Rate of Exchange (IROE) applicable at time of issuance. Used for consolidated ancillary revenue reporting, RASK/CASK analytics, and SAP S/4HANA FI ledger posting in functional currency.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Rate of Exchange (IROE); SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: exchange_emd_number
attributes.description: The 13-digit EMD number of the original document from which this EMD was exchanged/reissued. Null if this is an original issuance. Used for document lineage tracking, refund difference calculation, and BSP/ARC exchange reporting.

attributes.name: form_of_payment_detail
attributes.description: Masked payment instrument detail (e.g., last 4 digits of credit card, voucher number, check number). Full card numbers are NEVER stored per PCI DSS. Used for payment reconciliation and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; PCI DSS v4.0; IATA BSP Manual

attributes.name: form_of_payment_type
attributes.description: The type of payment instrument used to settle this EMD (e.g., credit_card, debit_card, cash, check, miles redemption, voucher, agency credit). Drives PCI compliance scope, BSP/ARC settlement method, and revenue accounting treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit_card|debit_card|cash|check|miles|voucher|agency_credit|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: gds_code
attributes.description: Two-character code identifying the Global Distribution System (GDS) through which the EMD was issued (e.g., 1A=Amadeus, 1S=Sabre, 1G=Galileo/Travelport, 1V=Worldspan). Null for direct channel sales. Used for GDS incentive reconciliation and distribution cost analytics.

attributes.name: interline_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this EMD involves an interline agreement (True), meaning the service may be delivered by a carrier other than the issuing airline. Drives interline proration, billing, and settlement processes.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Interline Traffic Agreements

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the EMD was issued to the passenger. The principal business event date for revenue recognition, BSP/ARC billing period assignment, and ancillary revenue reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: issue_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the EMD was issued in the Amadeus Altéa PSS or Sabre system. Used for audit trails, intraday revenue reporting, and IROP reissuance sequencing.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; Amadeus Altéa PSS; Sabre AirVision

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this EMD record in the lakehouse silver layer (e.g., status change from open to used, refund processing). Used for change data capture, audit trails, and downstream incremental processing.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

attributes.name: operating_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA designator of the airline actually operating the flight or delivering the service (may differ from issuing airline in codeshare or interline scenarios). Used for interline proration and service delivery accountability.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Airline Coding Directory

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code of the origin station for the associated flight segment (e.g., JFK, LHR). Used for route-level ancillary revenue analytics and geographic revenue attribution.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Airport Coding Directory

attributes.name: passenger_name
attributes.description: Full name of the passenger for whom the EMD was issued, in IATA surname/given-name format (e.g., 'SMITH/JOHN MR'). Required for passenger identification during service delivery and BSP/ARC settlement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; GDPR Article 4; IATA Resolution 722

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: The amount refunded to the passenger for this EMD in the transaction currency. Null if not refunded. Used for refund liability accounting, BSP/ARC debit memo processing, and DOT consumer protection compliance reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; DOT 14 CFR Part 259; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: refund_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which a refund was processed for this EMD. Null if not refunded. Used for refund liability tracking, BSP/ARC debit memo reconciliation, and DOT consumer protection reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; DOT 14 CFR Part 259

attributes.name: rfic
attributes.description: Single-character IATA Reason for Issuance Code (RFIC) classifying the broad category of ancillary service (e.g., A=Air Transportation, B=Surface Transportation, C=Baggage, D=Financial Impact, E=Airport Services, F=Merchandise, G=In-flight Services, I=Individual Airline Use). Used for BSP/ARC reporting and revenue categorisation.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA RFIC/RFISC Code List

attributes.name: rfisc
attributes.description: Three-character IATA Reason for Issuance Sub-Code (RFISC) providing granular classification of the ancillary service within the RFIC category (e.g., 0B5=Checked Baggage 1st Piece, 0CC=Seat Selection, 0B1=Priority Boarding). Used for ancillary revenue analytics, yield management, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA RFIC/RFISC Code List

attributes.name: sales_channel
attributes.description: The distribution channel through which the EMD was sold (e.g., direct_web, mobile_app, airport_kiosk, call_center, travel_agency, GDS, NDC, airport_counter). Used for ancillary revenue channel analytics and distribution cost management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: direct_web|mobile_app|airport_kiosk|call_center|travel_agency|gds|ndc|airport_counter — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: service_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which the ancillary service is to be delivered or consumed (e.g., flight date for excess baggage, lounge access date). May differ from issue_date for advance purchases. Used for revenue recognition scheduling and service fulfilment tracking.

attributes.name: service_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the ancillary service covered by this EMD (e.g., 'Excess Baggage 23kg', 'Seat Upgrade to Business Class', 'Airport Lounge Access', 'Priority Boarding', 'Pet in Cabin'). Sourced from the Sabre AirVision / Amadeus Altéa service catalogue.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA Ancillary Services Standard

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total taxes, fees, and surcharges applied to this EMD (e.g., Passenger Facility Charge (PFC), government taxes, carrier-imposed surcharges), in the transaction currency. Required for tax remittance, BSP/ARC settlement, and SAP S/4HANA FI tax accounting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; IRS; EASA; FAA

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: Total amount collected from the passenger for this EMD (base_amount + tax_amount), in the transaction currency. The gross revenue figure used for BSP/ARC settlement, SAP S/4HANA revenue posting, and ancillary revenue reporting.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: used_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the EMD coupon was lifted (service delivered). Null if status is not 'used'. Used for revenue recognition timing and service delivery confirmation.

attributes.name: void_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the EMD was voided (same-day cancellation before BSP/ARC lift). Null if not voided. Required for BSP/ARC void reporting and revenue reversal.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 636; IATA BSP Manual; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

products.name: bsp_settlement
products.description: BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan) settlement transaction record representing the financial settlement between the airline and travel agents through the IATA BSP clearing mechanism. Captures BSP billing period, agent IATA code, agent name, country/BSP market, transaction type (sale/refund/ADM/ACM), ticket number range, gross sales amount, commission amount, net remittance amount, currency, settlement date, BSP file reference, and settlement status (pending/settled/disputed/adjusted). SSOT for BSP-channel revenue collection and agent settlement.
products.reference: IATA BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan) / IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: bsp_settlement_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Billing and Settlement Plan (BSP) Settlement ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each BSP settlement transaction record in the airline's revenue management system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: BSP net remittance payments (airline paying net settlement to BSP or receiving from agents) generate AP entries for cash management and payment processing. IATA BSP reconciliation requires AP traceabi

attributes.name: agency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.agency. Business justification: bsp_settlement is a financial settlement transaction with a travel agency but currently stores only agent_iata_code (STRING) and agent_name (STRING) as denormalized references. Adding agency_id → reve

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: BSP settlements are reconciled to specific legal entities for cash management, AR/AP posting, and financial statement preparation. Core treasury and accounting process.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: BSP/ARC settlement is a major airline financial event requiring GL posting for gross sales, commissions, and net remittance. IATA BSP reconciliation and airline financial close processes require direc

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: BSP settlements are filed per reporting airline. Linking bsp_settlement to route.carrier enables carrier-level BSP reconciliation, IATA billing period analysis, and regulatory reporting. The airline_n

attributes.name: settlement_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: BSP settlements are processed and reconciled at specific stations; station FK enables settlement audit trails, station-level remittance tracking, and cost center allocation for settlement processing.

attributes.name: acm_amount
attributes.description: Total value of Agency Credit Memos (ACMs) issued to the travel agent in this settlement period. ACMs represent credits owed to the agent for airline-initiated corrections, overpayments, or goodwill adjustments. Positive value reduces agent liability.

attributes.name: adjustment_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier for any corrective adjustment applied to this BSP settlement. Populated when settlement_status is 'adjusted'. Links to the originating ADM, ACM, or manual journal entry in the revenue accounting system (SAP S/4HANA).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 854; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IATA BSP Operations Manual

attributes.name: adm_amount
attributes.description: Total value of Agency Debit Memos (ADMs) raised against the travel agent in this settlement period. ADMs recover amounts owed to the airline due to agent errors, fare violations, or unauthorized discounts. Positive value increases agent liability.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA ADM Policy; IATA Resolution 854

attributes.name: arc_report_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this BSP settlement to the corresponding ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation) settlement report for US-market transactions. Populated for settlements processed through ARC rather than IATA BSP. Used for dual-channel reconciliation.
attributes.references: ARC Industry Agent Handbook; DOT Revenue Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: billing_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the IATA BSP billing period covered by this settlement. Together with billing_period_start_date, defines the complete billing window for ticket sales included in this settlement.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: billing_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the IATA BSP billing period covered by this settlement. BSP billing periods are typically bi-monthly or monthly depending on the market. Defines the range of ticket sales included in this settlement.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: bsp_file_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Billing and Settlement Plan (BSP) File Reference
attributes.description: Externally-known IATA BSP file reference number assigned by the BSP clearing system to uniquely identify the settlement file batch. Used for reconciliation with IATA BSP reports and agent remittance matching.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: bsp_market_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code identifying the BSP market (country or territory) in which this settlement was processed. Determines the applicable BSP rules, currency, and remittance schedule.

attributes.name: commission_amount
attributes.description: Total commission amount deducted from gross sales and credited to the travel agent as per the applicable commission agreement. Reduces the net remittance amount owed to the airline.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: commission_rate
attributes.description: The percentage commission rate applied to the base fare to calculate the commission_amount for this settlement. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0100 = 1%). Determined by the airline-agent commission agreement and applicable IATA rules.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: SAP S/4HANA cost center code associated with the revenue management or sales function responsible for this BSP settlement. Used for internal financial reporting and P&L attribution by sales region or distribution channel.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IATA BSP Operations Manual

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this BSP settlement record was first captured in the airline's revenue management data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: dispute_raised_date
attributes.description: Date on which the dispute was formally raised against this BSP settlement by either the airline or the travel agent. Populated only when settlement_status is 'disputed'. Used to track dispute aging and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA ADM Policy

attributes.name: dispute_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized IATA or internal code describing the reason for a disputed BSP settlement. Populated only when settlement_status is 'disputed'. Used for dispute management, root cause analysis, and agent relationship management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FARE_DIFF|COMM_DISPUTE|TAX_ERROR|DUPLICATE|UNAUTH_REFUND|ADM_REJECT — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850; IATA ADM Policy

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the dispute for this BSP settlement was formally resolved. Populated when settlement_status transitions from 'disputed' to 'settled' or 'adjusted'. Used for dispute lifecycle reporting and agent relationship analytics.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA ADM Policy

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: Foreign exchange rate applied to convert the settlement amounts from the BSP market local currency to the airline's functional reporting currency (e.g., USD or EUR). Sourced from IATA Rate of Exchange (IROE) or the airline's treasury system.
attributes.references: IATA Rate of Exchange (IROE); ISO 4217; IFRS 21 Foreign Currency Transactions

attributes.name: gds_provider_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the Global Distribution System (GDS) through which the tickets in this settlement were issued. Common values: 1A (Amadeus), 1S (Sabre), 1G (Galileo/Travelport), 1V (Worldspan), 1P (Apollo). Used for channel analytics and GDS incentive reconciliation.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: gross_sales_amount
attributes.description: Total gross ticket sales value (fare + taxes + surcharges) billed to the travel agent in this BSP settlement period, before deduction of commissions or adjustments. Expressed in the settlement currency.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850; DOT Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: interline_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this BSP settlement includes interline ticket sales where the validating carrier is settling on behalf of one or more operating carriers under an interline ticketing agreement. True = interline settlement; False = single-carrier settlement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreements

attributes.name: ndc_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the tickets in this BSP settlement were issued via IATA New Distribution Capability (NDC) API channels rather than traditional GDS. True = NDC-sourced settlement; False = traditional GDS/BSP settlement. Used for NDC adoption tracking and distribution analytics.
attributes.references: IATA NDC Standard (IATA Resolution 787); IATA BSP Operations Manual

attributes.name: net_remittance_amount
attributes.description: Net amount remitted by the travel agent to the airline after deducting commissions and applying any ADM/ACM adjustments from gross sales. This is the actual cash settlement amount transferred through the BSP clearing mechanism.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850; DOT Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: pfc_amount
attributes.description: Total Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) amounts collected by the travel agent on behalf of US airports and included in this BSP settlement. PFCs are FAA-regulated charges that must be separately tracked and remitted to the relevant airport authorities.
attributes.references: FAA Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) Program; 14 CFR Part 158; DOT

attributes.name: remittance_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the travel agent is contractually required to remit the net settlement amount to the BSP clearing house. Determined by the BSP market remittance schedule. Used for cash flow forecasting and overdue tracking.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: sales_channel
attributes.description: The distribution channel through which the tickets in this BSP settlement were sold. Used for channel revenue analytics and distribution cost management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GDS|direct|online_travel_agency|corporate|consolidator|NDC — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA NDC Standard

attributes.name: settlement_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the BSP settlement amounts (gross sales, commission, net remittance) are denominated. Determined by the BSP market country and IATA currency rules.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The principal business event date on which the BSP clearing house executed the financial settlement and funds were remitted between the travel agent and the airline. Corresponds to the IATA BSP remittance date.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the BSP settlement transaction. 'pending' indicates awaiting clearing; 'settled' indicates funds remitted; 'disputed' indicates agent or airline has raised a discrepancy; 'adjusted' indicates a corrective entry has been applied; 'cancelled' indicates the settlement was voided.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total government taxes, airport fees, and fuel surcharges (YQ/YR) included in the gross sales amount. Taxes are collected by the agent on behalf of the airline and relevant authorities and must be separately tracked for regulatory remittance.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850; DOT; FAA Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) Rules

attributes.name: ticket_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual e-tickets included in this BSP settlement transaction. Used for volume reconciliation and agent productivity reporting.

attributes.name: ticket_number_range_end
attributes.description: The last e-ticket number in the range of tickets covered by this BSP settlement transaction. Together with ticket_number_range_start, defines the complete set of tickets included in this settlement batch.

attributes.name: ticket_number_range_start
attributes.description: The first e-ticket number in the range of tickets covered by this BSP settlement transaction. Follows IATA 13-digit ticket number format (3-digit airline code prefix + 10-digit serial). Used for reconciliation with the Passenger Service System (PSS).

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the BSP settlement transaction. 'sale' is a standard ticket sale; 'refund' is a passenger refund; 'ADM' (Agency Debit Memo) is a debit raised against the agent; 'ACM' (Agency Credit Memo) is a credit issued to the agent; 'reversal' is a correction of a prior transaction; 'adjustment' is a manual correction entry. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sale|refund|ADM|ACM|reversal|adjustment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA BSP Operations Manual; IATA Resolution 850; IATA Resolution 854

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this BSP settlement record was last modified in the airline's revenue management data platform. Tracks adjustments, status changes, and dispute resolutions.

products.name: recognition
products.description: Revenue accounting transaction record representing the recognized revenue entry for a flown or used ticket coupon or EMD. Captures the accounting period, ticket/coupon reference, flight date, origin-destination, cabin, booking class, fare amount recognized, prorate share (for interline), tax amounts, surcharges, form of payment, passenger type, revenue recognition method (flown/accrual), interline prorate agreement reference, and accounting status (pending/recognized/adjusted/reversed). SSOT for passenger revenue recognition aligned with IATA revenue accounting standards and airline financial reporting.
products.reference: IATA Revenue Accounting Manual (RAM) / IATA Resolution 743

attributes.name: recognition_id
attributes.description: Primary key for recognition

attributes.name: ancillary_emd_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ancillary.ancillary_emd. Business justification: Revenue recognition records must identify the source settlement document. For ancillary revenue (EMD-based), recognition must link to the ancillary_emd as the authoritative document. IFRS 15 and airli

attributes.name: bsp_settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.bsp_settlement. Business justification: Revenue recognition records track when revenue is recognized from flown/used tickets. The bsp_arc_report_period attribute indicates BSP settlement tracking. This should be a FK to the authoritative bs

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Revenue recognition must be attributed to a specific legal entity/company code for IFRS 15 segment reporting and multi-entity airline group consolidation. Regulators and auditors require recognition r

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Revenue is attributed to cost centers (routes, hubs, regions) for profitability analysis, management reporting, and route P&L. Standard airline financial management practice.

attributes.name: fare_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.fare. Business justification: Revenue recognition records capture the fare used for accounting recognition but currently store only fare_basis_code (STRING) with no FK to the fare master. Adding fare_id → revenue.fare.fare_id norm

attributes.name: flight_inventory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.flight_inventory. Business justification: Revenue accounting must tie recognized revenue to the specific flight inventory instance flown for accurate proration, interline settlement, and GL posting. Required for IFRS 15 compliance, matching r

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Revenue accounting records post to GL for IFRS 15 compliance and financial statement preparation. Core integration between revenue and finance systems.

attributes.name: interline_prorate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.interline_prorate. Business justification: Revenue recognition records for interline journeys should reference the prorate agreement that governs revenue sharing. The prorate_agreement_reference and interline_partner_code attributes in recogni

attributes.name: inventory_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.inventory_leg. Business justification: Leg-level revenue recognition and interline proration require direct reference to inventory_leg for per-leg capacity data. Recognition already links to flight_inventory (OD level) but airline revenue

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Each revenue recognition event under IFRS 15 generates a journal entry (debit deferred revenue, credit earned revenue). Airline revenue accounting systems require direct traceability from recognition

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: Revenue recognition for interline and codeshare flights requires identifying the operating carrier for prorate allocation and IFRS 15 revenue recognition. The operating_airline_code plain column is a

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Revenue accounting requires origin station FK for cost center allocation, station-level P&L reporting, interline settlement, and GL posting by station. Origin_airport_code is denormalized station refe

attributes.name: pnr_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservation.pnr. Business justification: Revenue recognition records must be traceable to the originating PNR for financial audit, revenue accounting reconciliation, and IFRS 15 compliance. recognition.pnr_locator is a denormalized reference

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Revenue accounting requires route-level attribution for prorate agreement application, bilateral settlement calculations, and P&L reporting by route. Route determines prorate factors, interline partne

attributes.name: technical_log_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.technical_log. Business justification: IFRS 15 revenue recognition for a flight segment requires confirmation that the service (flight) was actually performed and the aircraft was airworthy. Linking recognition to the technical log provide

attributes.name: ticket_coupon_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.ticket_coupon. Business justification: revenue_recognition records represent recognized revenue entries for flown or used travel. Each accounting record corresponds to one ticket coupon (flight segment). The table has ticket_number and cou

attributes.name: accounting_period
attributes.description: Financial accounting period (YYYY-MM) in which this revenue is recognized, aligned with the airline's fiscal calendar. Drives period-close reporting in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO and DOT financial filings.
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; IFRS 15; ASC 606

attributes.name: accounting_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of this revenue recognition record: PENDING (awaiting period-close processing), RECOGNIZED (revenue posted to GL), ADJUSTED (corrected after initial recognition), REVERSED (voided/cancelled entry), DISPUTED (under interline billing dispute).
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: adjustment_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for a revenue adjustment or reversal (e.g., IROP reprotection, involuntary downgrade, fare recalculation, interline dispute resolution). Populated only when accounting_status is ADJUSTED or REVERSED.
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; IATA Resolution 735

attributes.name: booking_class
attributes.description: Single-letter Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) representing the fare class/inventory bucket in which the ticket was booked (e.g., Y, B, M, Q, V). Drives yield management analysis and links to Sabre AirVision fare class buckets.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

attributes.name: cabin_class
attributes.description: IATA cabin class code indicating the physical cabin in which the passenger traveled: F (First), C (Business), W (Premium Economy), Y (Economy). Used for cabin-level revenue disaggregation and yield analysis.

attributes.name: codeshare_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this coupon was flown on a codeshare flight where the issuing carrier's flight number was marketed but operated by a partner airline. Affects revenue recognition treatment and interline settlement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 788 (Codeshare); DOT Codeshare Disclosure Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this revenue accounting record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and period-close reconciliation.
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the arrival station of the coupon segment. Combined with origin forms the O&D pair for revenue accounting and yield management analysis.

attributes.name: emd_number
attributes.description: IATA Electronic Miscellaneous Document number when this revenue recognition record relates to an ancillary service (e.g., excess baggage, seat upgrade, lounge access) rather than a flight coupon. Null for standard flight coupons.

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: IATA Rate of Exchange (IROE) applied to convert the fare from the ticketing currency to the settlement/reporting currency at the time of ticketing. Used for multi-currency revenue normalization in financial reporting.

attributes.name: fare_amount
attributes.description: Base fare amount recognized for this coupon in the settlement currency, excluding taxes and surcharges. For interline itineraries this is the prorated share allocated to this carrier. Core revenue figure for RASK and yield calculations.
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; IFRS 15; ASC 606

attributes.name: form_of_payment_type
attributes.description: Category of payment instrument used to purchase the ticket: CASH, CC (Credit Card), CHECK, VOUCHER, MILES (frequent flyer redemption), AGENCY (agency credit), OTHER. Drives revenue disaggregation between cash and non-cash revenue. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CASH|CC|CHECK|VOUCHER|MILES|AGENCY|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: fuel_surcharge_amount
attributes.description: Carrier-imposed fuel surcharge (IATA codes YQ for fuel surcharge, YR for carrier-imposed miscellaneous surcharge) collected on this coupon. Tracked separately for revenue accounting transparency and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728; DOT Surcharge Disclosure Rules

attributes.name: interline_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this coupon is part of an interline itinerary involving two or more carriers under an interline ticketing agreement. When true, prorate_amount and prorate_agreement_reference are applicable.

attributes.name: issuing_airline_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA designator of the airline that issued the ticket document. May differ from the operating carrier on codeshare or interline itineraries. Used to determine revenue accounting ownership.
attributes.references: IATA Airline Designator Standard; IATA Resolution 722

attributes.name: passenger_type_code
attributes.description: IATA Passenger Type Code indicating the category of traveler: ADT (Adult), CHD (Child), INF (Infant), MIL (Military), GOV (Government), STU (Student). Affects fare applicability and revenue disaggregation.

attributes.name: prorate_amount
attributes.description: The carrier's prorated share of the total through-fare for interline itineraries, calculated per the applicable IATA prorate agreement or bilateral prorate factor. Equals fare_amount for online (single-carrier) itineraries.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850 (Interline Revenue Accounting); IATA MITA

attributes.name: recognition_method
attributes.description: Method by which revenue is recognized for this record: FLOWN (recognized upon flight completion), ACCRUAL (deferred/accrual basis), PRORATE (interline prorate allocation), REDEMPTION (FFP miles redemption), REVERSAL (corrective reversal entry). Aligns with IFRS 15 performance obligation satisfaction.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; ASC 606; IATA Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: recognition_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this revenue recognition entry was processed and posted in the revenue accounting system. Represents the business event time of recognition, distinct from the flight date and the record audit timestamp.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; ASC 606; IATA Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: reporting_currency_amount
attributes.description: Fare amount converted to the airline's functional reporting currency (e.g., USD) using the IROE exchange rate. Used for consolidated financial reporting in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO and DOT/IATA statistical submissions.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; ASC 606; IATA Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: settlement_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the fare and surcharge amounts are denominated for BSP/ARC settlement (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Determines the settlement currency for interline billing.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; IATA BSP Settlement Rules; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating revenue accounting system (Sabre AirVision Revenue Management or SAP S/4HANA) for traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational system of record.
attributes.references: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Aggregate of all government-mandated taxes collected on this coupon (e.g., departure tax, VAT, PFC, segment tax). Reported separately from fare revenue per IATA revenue accounting standards and DOT reporting requirements.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728; DOT 14 CFR Part 399; IATA Revenue Accounting Standards

attributes.name: ticket_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the original ticket was issued. Used to determine the advance purchase window, applicable fare rules, and the deferred revenue liability period between ticketing and flight date.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this revenue accounting record (e.g., adjustment, status change, prorate recalculation). Used for incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: IATA Revenue Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI

products.name: interline_prorate
products.description: Interline prorate agreement and proration record defining how revenue from a multi-carrier itinerary is split between participating airlines. Captures prorate agreement type (IATA pro-rate factor/mileage/specific prorate agreement), partner carrier code, applicable route/market, prorate factor or amount, currency, effective and expiry dates, agreement reference number, and proration calculation method. Also stores actual proration transaction records for settled interline billing. Aligns with IATA interline billing and settlement standards.
products.reference: IATA Interline Prorate Agreement / IATA Resolution 743

attributes.name: interline_prorate_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each interline prorate agreement or proration transaction record in the silver layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: When our airline owes a prorate share to a partner carrier, an AP entry is created for settlement. IATA interline billing requires AP tracking for amounts payable to partner airlines. interline_prorat

attributes.name: bsp_settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.bsp_settlement. Business justification: Interline prorate settlements are processed through BSP channels. The settlement_period attribute indicates settlement tracking. This should be a FK to the authoritative bsp_settlement record. Standar

attributes.name: fare_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.fare. Business justification: interline_prorate records define how revenue from multi-carrier itineraries is split, and the proration is calculated based on specific fare constructions. Currently fare_basis_code (STRING) is stored

attributes.name: interline_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.interline_agreement. Business justification: Interline prorate calculations must be audited against the signed interline agreement (prorate basis, percentage, settlement terms). IATA revenue accounting standards require traceability from prorate

attributes.name: interline_billing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.interline_billing. Business justification: Prorate agreements drive interline billing transactions for settlement with partner airlines. Direct operational dependency for interline revenue accounting.

attributes.name: inventory_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.inventory_leg. Business justification: Interline proration is calculated per operated leg — each carrier's revenue share is based on their specific leg. interline_prorate has route_id and origin/destination but no inventory_leg_id. IATA pr

attributes.name: itinerary_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservation.itinerary_segment. Business justification: Interline proration is calculated per flight segment to allocate revenue between partner carriers. Linking to itinerary_segment enables segment-level interline revenue allocation, dispute resolution,

attributes.name: own_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: Interline prorate records must identify the own carrier (the airline running this system) linked to the authoritative carrier registry for IATA bilateral prorate audits and interline billing reconcili

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Prorate agreements are route-specific; route determines applicable bilateral ASA, traffic rights category, and revenue split methodology between operating and marketing carriers. Essential for interli

attributes.name: ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to revenue.ticket. Business justification: interline_prorate records define how revenue from multi-carrier itineraries is split between airlines. Each proration transaction references one ticket. The table has ticket_number (STRING) as a busin

attributes.name: agreement_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known reference number assigned to the interline prorate agreement, used for identification in IATA billing and settlement communications. Corresponds to the Specific Prorate Agreement (SPA) or IATA pro-rate factor agreement identifier. BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the interline prorate agreement: ACTIVE (in force), SUSPENDED (temporarily halted), EXPIRED (past effective period), TERMINATED (cancelled before expiry), PENDING (awaiting activation). LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interline prorate agreement method: SPA (Specific Prorate Agreement), IATA_PRF (IATA Pro-Rate Factor), MILEAGE (mileage-based proration), FIXED_AMOUNT (fixed monetary split), or PERCENTAGE (percentage-based split). CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

attributes.name: cabin_class
attributes.description: Cabin class to which this prorate agreement applies, restricting the agreement to a specific service level (e.g., FIRST, BUSINESS, PREMIUM_ECONOMY, ECONOMY). Null if the agreement applies to all cabin classes.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used to calculate the revenue proration between interline carriers: PROPORTIONAL (based on segment distance), EQUAL_SPLIT (equal share per carrier), MILEAGE_RATIO (IATA mileage-based), AGREED_FACTOR (bilaterally negotiated factor), FIXED (fixed amount per agreement). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PROPORTIONAL|EQUAL_SPLIT|MILEAGE_RATIO|AGREED_FACTOR|FIXED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: collected_fare_amount
attributes.description: Total fare amount collected from the passenger for the interline itinerary, in the settlement currency. This is the gross base amount from which the prorate split is calculated. MONETARY_TRIPLET — gross base amount.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA BSP Settlement Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline prorate record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the prorate amount or settlement value is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Applies to FIXED_AMOUNT and PERCENTAGE agreement types.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IATA Resolution 850; IATA BSP Settlement Standards

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the destination point of the interline route or market to which this prorate agreement applies.
attributes.references: IATA Airport Codes (IATA Resolution 763); ICAO Doc 7910

attributes.name: directionality
attributes.description: Indicates whether the prorate agreement applies to one-way (OW), round-trip (RT), or circle-trip (CT) itineraries. Aligns with IATA fare directionality conventions.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; ATPCO Fare Filing Standards

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the proration transaction or agreement is subject to an interline billing dispute: NONE (no dispute), DISPUTED (partner carrier has raised a dispute), UNDER_REVIEW (dispute under investigation), RESOLVED (dispute settled).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Billing Dispute Resolution Procedures

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the interline prorate agreement becomes binding and applicable to interline revenue splits. EFFECTIVE_FROM category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interline prorate agreement ceases to be binding. Null indicates an open-ended agreement with no defined termination date. EFFECTIVE_UNTIL category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: global_indicator
attributes.description: Two-letter IATA global indicator code defining the geographic routing area applicable to this prorate agreement (e.g., AT for Atlantic, PA for Pacific, AP for Asia-Pacific, EH for Eastern Hemisphere). Constrains the routing scope of the agreement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference — Global Indicators

attributes.name: iata_conference_area
attributes.description: IATA Traffic Conference area applicable to this prorate agreement: TC1 (Americas), TC2 (Europe, Middle East, Africa), TC3 (Asia-Pacific). Determines the IATA tariff conference jurisdiction governing the agreement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference — Traffic Conference Areas

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline prorate record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.

attributes.name: maximum_prorate_amount
attributes.description: Ceiling value for the prorate allocation in the agreement currency. Caps the carrier's revenue share to prevent over-recovery on high-yield itineraries under fixed-factor agreements.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: minimum_prorate_amount
attributes.description: Floor value for the prorate allocation in the agreement currency. Ensures the carrier receives at least this amount regardless of the calculated prorate factor or percentage. Protects against under-recovery on low-yield itineraries.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional remarks, special conditions, or negotiation notes associated with the interline prorate agreement or transaction. Used by revenue management analysts for context not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Interline Module

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the origin point of the interline route or market to which this prorate agreement applies.
attributes.references: IATA Airport Codes (IATA Resolution 763); ICAO Doc 7910

attributes.name: partner_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline designator code of the interline partner carrier participating in the prorate agreement. Identifies the counterparty airline for revenue split purposes.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 762 — Airline Designator Codes; IATA Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA)

attributes.name: passenger_type_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA Passenger Type Code (PTC) indicating the passenger category (e.g., ADT for adult, CHD for child, INF for infant) to which this prorate agreement applies. Null if applicable to all passenger types.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Passenger Type Codes

attributes.name: pnr_locator
attributes.description: Six-character alphanumeric Passenger Name Record (PNR) locator from the Amadeus Altéa PSS or GDS, linking the proration transaction to the passenger booking record.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 722; Amadeus Altéa PSS — PNR Standards

attributes.name: prorate_amount
attributes.description: Fixed monetary amount allocated to this carrier under the prorate agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Used for FIXED_AMOUNT agreement types where a specific dollar/currency value is agreed rather than a factor or percentage.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Billing and Settlement Plan (BSP)

attributes.name: prorate_basis
attributes.description: The underlying basis on which proration is computed: FARE (based on published fare components), MILEAGE (based on IATA TPM/MPM mileage), WEIGHT (cargo weight-based, for cargo interline), or REVENUE (based on actual collected revenue).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

attributes.name: prorate_factor
attributes.description: Numeric prorate factor (ratio) applied to the total fare to determine the revenue share allocated to this carrier's segment of the interline journey. Used for IATA_PRF and MILEAGE agreement types. Value between 0 and 1 representing the carrier's proportional share.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Pro-Rate Factor Methodology

attributes.name: prorate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the total interline fare revenue allocated to this carrier under the prorate agreement. Used for PERCENTAGE agreement types. Value between 0.0000 and 100.0000.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

attributes.name: prorated_revenue_amount
attributes.description: Net revenue amount allocated to the own carrier after applying the prorate factor, percentage, or fixed amount to the collected fare. This is the carrier's actual revenue share from the interline itinerary. MONETARY_TRIPLET — net total.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA BSP Settlement Standards; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

attributes.name: record_type
attributes.description: Discriminator indicating whether this record represents a prorate AGREEMENT (the standing agreement defining split rules) or a TRANSACTION (an actual proration event applied to a settled interline billing).
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; Sabre AirVision Revenue Management — Interline Module

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total taxes, fees, and surcharges (e.g., PFC, government taxes, fuel surcharges) associated with the interline proration transaction. Excluded from the prorate base fare calculation per IATA standards. MONETARY_TRIPLET — adjustment amount.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; DOT 14 CFR Part 399; IATA BSP Settlement Standards

attributes.name: ticketing_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline designator code of the carrier that issued the ticket for the interline itinerary. The ticketing carrier may differ from the operating carrier and determines BSP/ARC settlement responsibility.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA BSP Settlement Standards; ARC Industry Agents Handbook

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: Date on which the actual proration transaction was applied to a settled interline billing. Populated only for TRANSACTION record types; null for AGREEMENT records. BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA BSP Settlement Standards

attributes.name: via_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for an intermediate connecting point that further qualifies the applicable market for this prorate agreement. Null if the agreement applies to all routings between origin and destination.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 850; IATA Tariff Coordinating Conference

products.name: fare_family
products.description: Fare family (branded fare) master record defining a named bundle of fare conditions and ancillary inclusions marketed under a commercial brand name (e.g., Basic Economy, Standard, Flex, Business Lite, Business Plus). Captures fare family code, commercial brand name, cabin applicability, included services (carry-on baggage, checked baggage, seat selection, lounge access, miles accrual rate, change/refund conditions), fare class mapping, display priority, and marketing description. Enables branded fare merchandising across GDS, NDC, and direct channels.
products.reference: IATA Branded Fares / ATPCO Fare Families

attributes.name: fare_family_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the fare family (branded fare) record in the revenue management system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
