attributes.description: Identifier of the crew member holding this qualification. Links to crew member master record.

attributes.name: training_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.training_event. Business justification: A crew qualification (type rating, proficiency check result) is typically produced or validated by a specific training event (simulator check, OPC, PC). Linking qualification.training_event_id → train

attributes.name: check_type
attributes.description: Type of check or evaluation that resulted in this qualification: initial (first-time qualification), recurrent (periodic revalidation), upgrade (promotion to higher position), requalification (after lapse), line_check (operational line check). Null if not check-based.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this qualification record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Trail

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the qualification becomes valid and the crew member is authorized to operate under this qualification.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Qualification Module

attributes.name: endorsement_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of additional endorsements or restrictions on this qualification (e.g., ETOPS, CAT III, RNP AR, VFR only). Aligns with ICAO and FAA endorsement standards.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the qualification expires and is no longer valid. Null for qualifications without expiry (e.g., permanent endorsements).
attributes.references: FAA Part 61.56, FAA Part 117, EASA Part-FCL

attributes.name: flight_hours
attributes.description: Total flight hours logged under this qualification. Used for tracking experience and recency requirements.

attributes.name: is_pic_qualified
attributes.description: Indicates whether this qualification authorizes the crew member to act as Pilot in Command (PIC). True if PIC-qualified, False otherwise.

attributes.name: is_sic_qualified
attributes.description: Indicates whether this qualification authorizes the crew member to act as Second in Command (SIC). True if SIC-qualified, False otherwise.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Date the qualification was originally issued or granted to the crew member.

attributes.name: landings_count
attributes.description: Total number of landings performed under this qualification. Critical for recency requirements (e.g., 3 takeoffs and landings in 90 days).

attributes.name: last_check_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent proficiency check, simulator check, or line check for this qualification. Used to track recency and currency.

attributes.name: last_flight_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent flight operated under this qualification. Used to determine recency and currency status.

attributes.name: medical_class
attributes.description: Class of medical certificate required or held for this qualification: class_1 (airline transport pilot), class_2 (commercial pilot), class_3 (private pilot). Null for cabin crew qualifications.

attributes.name: next_check_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next proficiency check or recurrent training must be completed to maintain qualification currency.

attributes.name: position_code
attributes.description: Crew position this qualification authorizes: CA (Captain), FO (First Officer), SO (Second Officer), CP (Co-Pilot), FA (Flight Attendant), PS (Purser), LS (Lead Steward). Null for non-position qualifications.
attributes.references: IATA Crew Position Codes, AIMS Crew Management System

attributes.name: qualification_category
attributes.description: High-level category of the qualification: type_rating (aircraft type), position_authorization (Captain, FO, Purser), endorsement (ICAO/FAA licence endorsement), recurrent_training (annual recurrency), special_qualification (ETOPS, CAT III), medical_certificate (Class 1/2 medical).
attributes.references: FAA Part 61, EASA Part-FCL, ICAO Annex 1

attributes.name: qualification_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the qualification type (e.g., B737, A320, B777, PURSER, FA). Aligns with ICAO and FAA type rating nomenclature.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 1 - Personnel Licensing, FAA Part 61

attributes.name: qualification_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the qualification (e.g., Boeing 737-800 Type Rating, Airbus A320 Family Type Rating, Purser Qualification).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Qualification Module

attributes.name: qualification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the qualification: current (valid and active), expired (past expiry date), suspended (temporarily invalid), revoked (permanently invalid), pending (awaiting approval), in_training (training in progress).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Qualification Module

attributes.name: recency_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member meets recency requirements for this qualification: current (meets all recency rules), expiring_soon (within alert window), expired (recency lapsed), not_applicable (no recency requirement).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes or comments about this qualification, including special circumstances, waivers, or administrative notes.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Qualification Module

attributes.name: restrictions
attributes.description: Free-text description of any operational restrictions or limitations on this qualification (e.g., VFR only, daylight operations only, supervised operations required).

attributes.name: simulator_hours
attributes.description: Total simulator training hours logged for this qualification. Used for tracking training investment and proficiency.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Training Module

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this qualification record was last modified in the system.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Trail

products.name: base
products.description: Reference master for crew domicile bases — the home airports from which crew are assigned, rostered, and begin/end pairings. Captures IATA/ICAO airport code, base name, crew categories served (flight deck, cabin, or both), base capacity (authorized headcount by category), base manager, operational timezone, and associated rest facilities. Used as the anchor point for pairing construction (pairings start/end at base), deadhead planning, reserve pool sizing, and crew positioning decisions. The SSOT for crew base definitions within the crew domain. Aligns with AIMS base management module.
products.reference: AIMS Crew Management — Base Management

attributes.name: base_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crew base. Primary key for the crew base reference master.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: FK to finance.cost_centre

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: Crew bases operate under a specific carrier's AOC (Air Operator Certificate). Linking base to carrier enables regulatory compliance reporting (which AOC governs each base), wet-lease crew management,

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Every crew base is physically located at an airport station. Crew base management, slot coordination, and ground handling reports require a formal FK linking the base to its station. icao_code on base

attributes.name: base_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the crew domicile base (e.g., JFK, LAX, ORD). This is the operational identifier used in crew scheduling and pairing construction.

attributes.name: base_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the crew base (e.g., 'New York JFK Base', 'Los Angeles International Base'). Human-readable identifier for business users.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: base_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the crew base. Active = fully operational, Inactive = temporarily not staffed, Seasonal = operates during specific periods, Temporary = short-term base, Closed = permanently shut down.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: base_type
attributes.description: Classification of the crew base by operational role within the network (hub = major connecting base, spoke = destination base, regional = regional operations, international = international crew base, domestic = domestic-only operations, satellite = secondary base).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: cabin_crew_capacity
attributes.description: Authorized headcount for cabin crew (flight attendants) assigned to this base. Used for crew planning, reserve pool sizing, and capacity management.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Primary email address for the crew base operations office. Used for crew communication, scheduling notifications, and administrative correspondence.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for the crew base operations office. Used for crew communication, scheduling coordination, and operational support.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the base location (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Used for regulatory compliance, labor law application, and crew work permit validation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew base record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: crew_categories_served
attributes.description: Indicates which crew categories are domiciled at this base (flight_deck_only = pilots only, cabin_crew_only = flight attendants only, both = pilots and cabin crew, all = all crew types including ground crew).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: crew_training_facility_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether crew training facilities (simulators, classrooms, recurrent training) are available at or near this base. Impacts crew recency management and type rating maintenance.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Training Management Module

attributes.name: current_cabin_crew_count
attributes.description: Current actual number of cabin crew members assigned to this base. Used to calculate staffing gaps and utilization.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: current_flight_deck_count
attributes.description: Current actual number of flight deck crew members assigned to this base. Used to calculate staffing gaps and utilization.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: deadhead_positioning_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether crew can be deadheaded (repositioned without revenue duty) to or from this base. Used in crew positioning decisions and irregular operations recovery.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Crew Positioning Module

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this crew base became operational and available for crew assignments and pairing construction. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: flight_deck_capacity
attributes.description: Authorized headcount for flight deck crew (pilots) assigned to this base. Used for crew planning, reserve pool sizing, and capacity management.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: ftl_regulation_applicable
attributes.description: Specific flight time limitations and rest requirements regulation applicable to crew based at this location (FAR_117 = US FAR Part 117, EASA_FTL = EASA Flight Time Limitations, CAP_371 = UK CAA Flight Time Limitations, other = jurisdiction-specific regulations).
attributes.references: FAR Part 117, EASA FTL (EU Regulation 83/2014), CAP 371

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew base record was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special instructions, or base-specific considerations relevant to crew scheduling and operations.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: operational_timezone
attributes.description: IANA timezone identifier for the crew base location (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'America/Los_Angeles'). Used for duty period calculations, rest requirement enforcement, and fatigue risk management per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

attributes.name: pairing_start_end_base
attributes.description: Indicates whether this base is used as a start/end point for crew pairings. True = pairings are constructed to begin and end at this base, False = crew may be positioned but pairings do not originate here.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Construction Module

attributes.name: physical_address
attributes.description: Full physical address of the crew base operations office or crew reporting location. Used for crew reporting instructions and facility management.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: reserve_pool_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a reserve crew pool is maintained at this base for operational contingencies, irregular operations, and last-minute crew substitutions.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Reserve Management Module

attributes.name: reserve_pool_size_cabin
attributes.description: Target number of cabin crew members to maintain in reserve status at this base. Used for reserve pool sizing and crew resource allocation.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Reserve Management Module

attributes.name: reserve_pool_size_flight_deck
attributes.description: Target number of flight deck crew members to maintain in reserve status at this base. Used for reserve pool sizing and crew resource allocation.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Reserve Management Module

attributes.name: rest_facility_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether crew rest facilities are available at this base for pre-duty rest, post-duty rest, or reserve crew standby. Critical for fatigue risk management and crew legality checks.
attributes.references: FAR Part 117 - Flight and Duty Limitations and Rest Requirements, EASA FTL

attributes.name: rest_facility_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of crew members that can be accommodated simultaneously in the base rest facilities. Used for reserve crew planning and irregular operations (IROP) management.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: rest_facility_type
attributes.description: Type of rest facility available at the base (hotel = contracted hotel rooms, crew_lounge = airport crew lounge, dedicated_facility = airline-owned rest facility, none = no rest facility).
attributes.references: FAR Part 117 - Flight and Duty Limitations and Rest Requirements, EASA FTL

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date when this crew base was closed or deactivated. Null for active bases. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Management Module

attributes.name: utc_offset_hours
attributes.description: Standard UTC offset in hours for the base location (e.g., -5.00 for EST, -8.00 for PST). Used for time zone conversions in crew scheduling and pairing construction.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

products.name: pairing
products.description: A crew pairing (also called a trip or rotation) is the core operational scheduling unit — a sequence of duty periods and rest periods starting and ending at the same crew base, built during the schedule construction phase. Captures pairing code, base, effective date range, total block hours, total duty time, total credit hours, number of legs, overnight stations, and pairing cost. Pairings are the output of the crew pairing optimizer and the input to rostering. Aligns with AIMS pairing module.
products.reference: AIMS Crew Management — Pairing Module / Jeppesen Crew Pairing

attributes.name: pairing_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crew pairing (trip or rotation). Primary key.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Pairings are constructed for specific aircraft types in crew scheduling optimization. PBS systems must match crew qualifications to pairing aircraft types. Essential for legal crew assignment and sche

attributes.name: base_id
attributes.description: Reference to the crew base (domicile) where this pairing starts and ends. All pairings are round-trip from a single base.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Base Module

attributes.name: block_time_standard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.block_time_standard. Business justification: Block time standards define planned block times used in FTL legality calculations for pairings. Linking pairing to block_time_standard enables validation of pairing total_block_hours against route sta

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Pairings generate crew costs allocated to cost centres for route profitability analysis, operational cost tracking, and unit cost (CASK) calculation. Essential for flight-level P&L and hub economics.

attributes.name: fleet_assignment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.fleet_assignment. Business justification: Crew pairings must be validated against fleet assignments to ensure crew qualifications match the assigned aircraft type on each route-season combination. This link enables crew planners to directly v

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to flight.flight_leg. Business justification: Pairings are multi-leg crew duty sequences; operations control, crew tracking, and actual-vs-planned analysis require resolving which specific flight_leg instances comprise each pairing. This enables

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Pairings originate from specific stations where crew report for duty. Critical for crew scheduling optimization, deadhead planning, and ensuring crew base alignment with operational requirements.

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Crew cost-per-route reporting and network crew planning require pairings to be directly attributed to routes. Crew planners build pairings for specific route operations; this link enables route-level

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: Crew pairings are constructed per IATA schedule season. Linking pairing to schedule_season enables season-level crew cost analysis, pairing reuse across equivalent seasons, and alignment with the netw

attributes.name: seasonal_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.seasonal_schedule. Business justification: Pairings are constructed to cover specific seasonal schedule operations. Linking pairing to seasonal_schedule enables crew planners to trace which scheduled service pattern a pairing covers, supportin

attributes.name: cost
attributes.description: Estimated total cost of operating this pairing, including crew pay, per diem, hotel, transportation, and deadhead costs. Used by the pairing optimizer for cost minimization.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the pairing cost (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing record was first created in the system. Audit field for record creation tracking.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Standards

attributes.name: crew_position
attributes.description: The crew position or role this pairing is designed for (captain, first officer, flight attendant, purser, relief pilot). Determines qualification and legality requirements.

attributes.name: deadhead_segments
attributes.description: Count of deadhead (non-revenue positioning) segments in this pairing where crew travel as passengers to reposition for operational duty.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The last date this pairing is valid for crew assignment. End of the pairing's operational window. Nullable for open-ended pairings.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The first date this pairing is valid and available for crew assignment. Start of the pairing's operational window.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: end_datetime
attributes.description: The scheduled date and time when the pairing ends (crew release time at base). Represents the end of the last duty period.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated fatigue risk score for this pairing based on duty patterns, circadian disruption, and rest opportunities. Used in Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS). Higher scores indicate higher fatigue risk.

attributes.name: hotel_cost
attributes.description: Estimated total hotel accommodation cost for all layovers in this pairing. Used for pairing cost calculation.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: international_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing includes any international (cross-border) flight legs. True if any leg crosses international boundaries, false if all legs are domestic.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Standards

attributes.name: legality_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing meets all regulatory crew duty and rest requirements (legal), violates regulations (illegal), is under review (pending_review), or has an approved waiver (waiver_approved).

attributes.name: max_duty_period_hours
attributes.description: The longest single duty period (in hours) within this pairing. Used to verify compliance with FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL maximum duty limits.

attributes.name: min_rest_period_hours
attributes.description: The shortest rest period (in hours) within this pairing. Must meet or exceed minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or comments about this pairing (e.g., special qualifications required, known issues, crew preferences).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: number_of_duty_periods
attributes.description: Total count of duty periods in this pairing. A duty period is a continuous block of work time from crew report to crew release, separated by rest periods.

attributes.name: number_of_layovers
attributes.description: Total count of overnight layovers (rest periods away from base) in this pairing. Each layover occurs at an overnight station.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: number_of_legs
attributes.description: Total count of flight legs (segments) included in this pairing. Each leg is a single takeoff-to-landing flight.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: optimization_run_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific optimization run that produced this pairing. Links pairing to the batch optimization process.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: optimizer_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the crew pairing optimizer software that generated this pairing. Used for audit and reproducibility.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: overnight_stations
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA airport codes where crew have overnight layovers during this pairing (e.g., 'JFK,LAX,ORD'). Sequence reflects pairing order.

attributes.name: pairing_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the pairing, externally known code used in crew scheduling and operations. Typically alphanumeric format assigned by the pairing optimizer.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: pairing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pairing: draft (under construction), published (available for assignment), assigned (crew assigned), in_progress (currently being flown), completed (finished), cancelled (no longer valid).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: pairing_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pairing based on route characteristics: domestic (all legs within one country), international (crosses borders), mixed (combination), reserve (standby duty), training (instructional flights), or positioning (deadhead crew movement).

attributes.name: per_diem_amount
attributes.description: Total per diem allowance payable to crew for this pairing, covering meals and incidental expenses during layovers. Calculated per CBA rules.

attributes.name: premium_pay_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing qualifies for premium pay under CBA rules (e.g., due to red-eye flights, long duty periods, or undesirable layovers). True if premium pay applies.

attributes.name: published_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing was published and made available for crew assignment. Nullable if pairing has not yet been published.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: red_eye_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing includes any red-eye (overnight) flights that operate during typical sleep hours (typically 10 PM to 6 AM). True if any leg is a red-eye flight.

attributes.name: start_datetime
attributes.description: The scheduled date and time when the pairing begins (crew report time at base). Represents the start of the first duty period.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: time_away_from_base_hours
attributes.description: Total elapsed time from pairing start to pairing end, representing how long crew are away from their base. Includes duty time, rest time, and layover time. Key quality-of-life metric.

attributes.name: total_block_hours
attributes.description: Total flight time (block hours) accumulated across all legs in this pairing, measured from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks). Used for crew pay and legality checks.

attributes.name: total_credit_hours
attributes.description: Total pay credit hours for this pairing, calculated per collective bargaining agreement rules. May differ from block hours due to minimum guarantees, premiums, and duty rigs.

attributes.name: total_duty_hours
attributes.description: Total duty time across all duty periods in this pairing, from crew report to crew release. Includes flight time, ground time, and pre/post-flight duties. Subject to FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL limits.

attributes.name: total_rest_hours
attributes.description: Total rest time provided across all rest periods in this pairing. Must meet minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

products.name: duty_period
products.description: A duty period is a continuous block of time during which a crew member is on duty, bounded by report time and release time. Belongs to a pairing. Captures report time, release time, total duty elapsed time (TDT), flight duty period (FDP) start/end, rest period before and after, duty type (flight duty, ground duty, deadhead, training), and FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL legality status. The atomic unit for fatigue risk and FTL compliance calculations.
products.reference: FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL — Flight Duty Period

attributes.name: duty_period_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the duty period. Primary key.

attributes.name: base_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.crew_base. Business justification: Normalize duty_period to reference crew_base by FK. Currently duty_period stores crew_base_code (STRING) as a denormalized reference to the crew's home base for the duty period. Adding crew_base_id FK

attributes.name: duty_cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Duty periods drive crew cost allocation for flight-level P&L, activity-based costing, and cost centre reporting. Supports detailed operational cost analysis and variance reporting against budget.

attributes.name: duty_start_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: FTL compliance reporting and crew positioning require duty periods to be formally anchored to their start station. Aviation regulators and crew control systems track where each duty period originates.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Duty Period General Ledger Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Duty periods drive FDP pay, augmented crew allowances, and split-duty payments posted to GL. Airline payroll-to-GL reconciliation requires duty_period→GL traceability. Aviation finance controllers exp

attributes.name: member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the crew member assigned to this duty period.

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Occurrences happen during specific duty periods. Essential for fatigue analysis, FTL investigation, and causal factor determination. Real business process: occurrence context analysis and fatigue risk

attributes.name: pairing_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pairing that contains this duty period. A pairing is a sequence of duty periods and rest periods assigned to a crew member.

attributes.name: acclimation_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member is acclimated to the local time zone at duty start. Acclimated means the crew member has been in the time zone for sufficient time per FAR Part 117 definitions. Affects maximum FDP limits.

attributes.name: actual_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period was actually operated (True) or was planned but not executed (False). Used for payroll and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: augmented_crew_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period involves augmented crew (additional crew members allowing in-flight rest). True if augmented, False otherwise. Affects maximum FDP limits.

attributes.name: block_hours_minutes
attributes.description: Total block time (gate departure to gate arrival) in minutes for all flight segments within this duty period. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating why the duty period was cancelled if actual_flag is False (e.g., CREW_SICK, AIRCRAFT_MAINTENANCE, WEATHER, SCHEDULE_CHANGE). Null if duty was operated.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this duty period record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: duty_end_station_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code where the duty period ends (release location).

attributes.name: duty_period_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of this duty period within the pairing (1, 2, 3, etc.).

attributes.name: duty_type
attributes.description: Classification of the duty period: flight duty (operating flights), ground duty (administrative/ground tasks), deadhead (crew repositioning without revenue duty), training (simulator/classroom), standby (on-call at airport), or reserve (on-call at home/hotel).

attributes.name: easa_ftl_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Flight Time Limitations (FTL) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period is compliant with EASA FTL regulations. True if compliant, False if violation detected.

attributes.name: far_117_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Aviation Regulation (FAR) Part 117 Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period is compliant with FAA FAR Part 117 flight and duty time limitations. True if compliant, False if violation detected.

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_level
attributes.description: Categorical fatigue risk level derived from the fatigue risk score: low (acceptable), moderate (monitor), high (mitigate), critical (unacceptable).

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated fatigue risk score for this duty period based on biomathematical fatigue models (e.g., SAFTE-FAST, Boeing Alertness Model). Higher scores indicate higher fatigue risk. Scale typically 0-100.

attributes.name: fdp_elapsed_time_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flight Duty Period (FDP) Elapsed Time in Minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes from FDP start to FDP end. Critical for FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL maximum FDP limit checks. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: fdp_end_time
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the end of the flight duty period, which ends when the aircraft finally comes to rest and the engines are shut down at the last flight segment. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: fdp_start_time

products.name: roster

products.name: ftl_legality_check
products.description: Unified crew fitness-to-operate assessment records encompassing both regulatory FTL/FDP legality checks (FAR Part 117, EASA FTL) and biomathematical fatigue risk model assessments (SAFE, FAID, FRMS). Each record captures: check timestamp, crew member, duty period or pairing evaluated, assessment method (regulatory_rule or biomathematical_model), regulation/model applied, check trigger (pre-assignment, pre-departure, post-duty, IROP extension), cumulative flight time windows (28-day, 365-day), FDP limit and actual FDP, rest compliance status, fatigue score and risk band (for model-based), mitigations applied, approving authority, and overall fitness result (legal/illegal/waiver/elevated-risk). The SSOT for crew legality and fatigue risk audit trail. Supports SMS, FRMS (ICAO Doc 9966), and regulatory compliance.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: FTL violations are a primary causal factor in fatigue-related safety occurrences. EASA ORO.FTL and FAR Part 117 require linking FTL breaches to safety events. ftl_legality_check has no occurrence link

attributes.name: pairing_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the crew pairing being evaluated. Nullable if check is duty-period-level.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the check result, waiver, or mitigation was approved by the authority. Nullable for automated pass results.

attributes.name: approving_authority
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authority who approved the check result, waiver, or mitigation (e.g., Crew Control Manager, Chief Pilot, Duty Manager). Nullable for automated pass results.

attributes.name: assessment_method
attributes.description: Method used for the fitness assessment: regulatory_rule (FAR Part 117, EASA FTL rule-based check) or biomathematical_model (SAFE, FAID, FRMS model-based fatigue risk assessment).
attributes.references: FAR Part 117, EASA FTL, ICAO Doc 9966

attributes.name: check_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding the legality check, including rationale for waivers, mitigation details, or special circumstances. Nullable if no additional context required.

attributes.name: check_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the FTL legality or fatigue risk check was executed.

attributes.name: check_trigger
attributes.description: Event or condition that triggered the legality check: pre-assignment (during rostering), pre-departure (gate check), post-duty (compliance audit), IROP extension (irregular operations duty extension request), manual audit, or scheduled review.
attributes.references: FAR Part 117, EASA FTL, ICAO Doc 9966

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_band
attributes.description: Categorical fatigue risk band derived from the fatigue score: low, moderate, elevated, high, or critical. Nullable for regulatory rule-based checks.

attributes.name: fatigue_score
attributes.description: Numeric fatigue risk score generated by the biomathematical model (e.g., SAFE effectiveness score, FAID fatigue index). Nullable for regulatory rule-based checks.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9966 (FRMS), SAFE Model, FAID Quantum

attributes.name: fdp_actual_hours
attributes.description: Actual or projected FDP duration in hours for the duty period being evaluated.

attributes.name: fdp_limit_hours
attributes.description: Maximum allowable FDP duration in hours per the applicable regulation, adjusted for number of sectors, time of day, and crew augmentation.

attributes.name: fitness_result
attributes.description: Overall fitness-to-operate result: legal (crew is legal and fit), illegal (crew exceeds FTL limits), waiver_granted (regulatory waiver issued for non-compliance), or elevated_risk_accepted (biomathematical model shows elevated risk but accepted with mitigation).
attributes.references: FAR Part 117, EASA FTL, ICAO Doc 9966 (FRMS)

attributes.name: flight_time_28_day
attributes.description: Cumulative flight time in hours for the crew member over the preceding 28-day rolling window at the time of check.

attributes.name: flight_time_365_day
attributes.description: Cumulative flight time in hours for the crew member over the preceding 365-day rolling window at the time of check.

attributes.name: mitigation_applied
attributes.description: Description of any mitigation measures applied to address elevated fatigue risk or legality concerns (e.g., crew augmentation, duty period reduction, additional rest, flight reassignment). Nullable if no mitigation required.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this legality check record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this legality check record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: rest_compliance_status
attributes.description: Status of rest period compliance: compliant (meets minimum), non_compliant (below minimum), reduced_rest_approved (approved reduced rest per regulation), or waiver_granted (regulatory waiver issued).

attributes.name: rest_period_actual_hours
attributes.description: Actual rest period in hours provided or projected before the next duty period.

attributes.name: rest_period_required_hours
attributes.description: Minimum rest period required in hours before the next duty period per applicable regulation.

attributes.name: system_source
attributes.description: Source system or module that generated the legality check record (e.g., AIMS Crew Management System, SAFE Model Engine, FAID Quantum, Manual Entry).

Captures training type, aircraft type, training date, training centre, instructor, result (pass/fail/incomplete), and next due date. The SSOT for crew training history and upcoming training requirements. Aligns with AIMS training module.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft. Business justification: Line checks and OE (operating experience) flights require recording the specific tail number used. Regulatory authorities (FAA, EASA) require tail-specific traceability for line check records. The exi

attributes.name: training_cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Training events are significant cost items allocated to training cost centres for budget tracking, cost recovery, and regulatory compliance reporting. Essential for training cost management and financ

attributes.name: training_result_code

attributes.name: training_score
attributes.description: Numerical score or grade achieved in the training event, if applicable. Null for pass/fail only training.

attributes.name: training_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the training session began.

attributes.name: training_status
attributes.description: Current status of the training event in its lifecycle. SCHEDULED=Planned but not started, IN_PROGRESS=Currently underway, COMPLETED=Finished, CANCELLED=Event cancelled, NO_SHOW=Crew member did not attend.

attributes.name: training_syllabus_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the training syllabus or curriculum used for this event.

attributes.name: training_type_code
attributes.description: Code representing the type of training event. PC=Proficiency Check, OPC=Operator Proficiency Check, LOE=Line Operational Evaluation, EPT=Emergency Procedures Training, CRM=Crew Resource Management, ETOPS=Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards, DG=Dangerous Goods, SEC=Security Training, GND=Ground Training, DIFF=Differences Training, RECUR=Recurrent Training. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PC|OPC|LOE|EPT|CRM|ETOPS|DG|SEC|GND|DIFF|RECUR — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: validity_end_date

attributes.name: validity_start_date

products.name: medical_certificate
products.description: Crew medical certificate records tracking ICAO Class 1 (flight crew) and Class 2 (cabin crew) medical certificates. Captures certificate class, issuing authority (AME/DAME), issue date, expiry date, certificate number, any limitations or waivers, and current validity status. Critical for crew legality — a crew member cannot operate without a valid medical certificate. Aligns with FAA/EASA medical certification requirements.
products.reference: ICAO Annex 1 — Personnel Licensing / FAR Part 67 / EASA Part-MED

attributes.name: medical_certificate_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crew medical certificate record. Primary key.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Certificate Accounts Payable Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Aviation medical examiners invoice airlines for mandatory crew medical examinations. Linking medical_certificate to AP enables matching of examination records to vendor invoices — required for crew co

attributes.name: member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the crew member to whom this medical certificate belongs. Links to crew member master record.

attributes.name: certificate_class
attributes.description: ICAO medical certificate class. Class 1 for airline transport pilots and commercial pilots, Class 2 for private pilots and cabin crew, Class 3 for air traffic controllers.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 1, FAA Part 67, EASA Part-MED

attributes.name: certificate_number
attributes.description: Unique certificate number issued by the Aviation Medical Examiner (AME) or Designated Aviation Medical Examiner (DAME). Official identifier for regulatory tracking.

attributes.name: certificate_type
attributes.description: Type of medical certificate issuance. Initial for first-time, Renewal for standard periodic renewal, Revalidation for extension, Special Issuance for conditional approval with limitations or waivers.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this medical certificate record was first created in the AIMS Crew Management System.

attributes.name: document_reference_url
attributes.description: URL or file path reference to the scanned or digital copy of the physical medical certificate document stored in the document management system.

attributes.name: examination_date
attributes.description: Date the crew member underwent the medical examination that resulted in this certificate issuance. May differ from issue date if additional review or approval was required.

attributes.name: examination_type
attributes.description: Type of medical examination conducted. Standard for routine periodic examinations, Extended for comprehensive examinations with additional tests, Special for examinations required due to medical events or regulatory requests.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date the medical certificate expires. Crew member cannot operate beyond this date without a valid renewed certificate. Critical for crew legality checks.
attributes.references: FAA Part 67, EASA Part-MED, ICAO Annex 1

attributes.name: hearing_aid_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member requires a hearing aid to meet hearing standards. True if hearing aid is required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Date the medical certificate was issued by the Aviation Medical Examiner (AME) or Designated Aviation Medical Examiner (DAME).

attributes.name: issuing_authority_license_number
attributes.description: License or designation number of the Aviation Medical Examiner (AME) or Designated Aviation Medical Examiner (DAME) who issued the certificate. Used for regulatory verification.

attributes.name: issuing_authority_name
attributes.description: Name of the Aviation Medical Examiner (AME) or Designated Aviation Medical Examiner (DAME) who issued the certificate.

attributes.name: issuing_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the medical certificate was issued. Determines applicable regulatory authority (FAA, EASA, etc.).

attributes.name: limitations
attributes.description: Any operational limitations or restrictions imposed on the crew member as a condition of the medical certificate. Examples include corrective lenses required, valid only with co-pilot, daytime operations only, or specific medical monitoring requirements.

attributes.name: next_examination_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the crew member must undergo the next medical examination to maintain continuous medical certification. Used for proactive crew scheduling and compliance planning.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional remarks, notes, or comments from the Aviation Medical Examiner (AME) or regulatory authority regarding the medical certificate. May include follow-up requirements, monitoring instructions, or clarifications.

attributes.name: special_issuance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certificate was issued under special issuance provisions due to a medical condition that does not meet standard requirements but has been granted a waiver or authorization. True if special issuance, False for standard issuance.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this medical certificate record was last updated in the AIMS Crew Management System. Tracks any modifications to certificate details, status changes, or verification updates.

attributes.name: validity_status
attributes.description: Current validity status of the medical certificate. Valid indicates the certificate is active and within its validity period. Expired indicates the certificate has passed its expiry date. Suspended or Revoked indicates regulatory action. Pending indicates awaiting final approval or special issuance decision.

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: Date the medical certificate was last verified with the issuing regulatory authority or through the AIMS Crew Management System.

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Status of verification of the medical certificate with the issuing regulatory authority. Verified indicates the certificate has been confirmed as authentic and valid with the authority. Used for compliance audits and crew legality validation.

attributes.name: vision_corrected_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member requires corrective lenses (glasses or contact lenses) to meet vision standards. True if corrective lenses are required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: waivers
attributes.description: Any medical waivers or special issuance conditions granted by the regulatory authority. Indicates exceptions to standard medical requirements with documented justification.

products.name: licence
products.description: Crew aviation licence master records — ATPL (Airline Transport Pilot Licence), CPL (Commercial Pilot Licence), MPL (Multi-crew Pilot Licence), and cabin crew attestation/licence. Captures licence number, issuing authority (FAA, EASA, national CAA), licence type, issue date, ratings held, language proficiency endorsement (ICAO level), and current validity. Distinct from qualification (which tracks type ratings and currency) — this is the base legal authorisation to act as crew.
products.reference: ICAO Annex 1 — Personnel Licensing / FAR Part 61 / EASA Part-FCL

attributes.name: licence_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crew aviation licence record. Primary key.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id

attributes.name: medical_certificate_id

attributes.name: member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the crew member who holds this licence.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this licence record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the scanned or electronic copy of the licence document stored in the document management system.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the licence expires and is no longer valid unless renewed. Null if the licence has no expiration (lifetime validity).

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the licence was originally issued by the regulatory authority.

attributes.name: language_proficiency_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the language proficiency endorsement expires and must be re-assessed. Null if no expiry (level 6 Expert has no expiry).

attributes.name: language_proficiency_level
attributes.description: ICAO language proficiency rating for aviation English (or other endorsed language). Scale 1-6, where 4 (Operational) is the minimum for international operations, 6 is Expert. Per ICAO Annex 1.

attributes.name: licence_number
attributes.description: The unique licence number issued by the regulatory authority. This is the official identifier on the physical or electronic licence document.

attributes.name: licence_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the licence: valid (active and in good standing), expired (past expiry date), suspended (temporarily invalid), revoked (permanently cancelled), pending_renewal (renewal in process), surrendered (voluntarily returned).

attributes.name: licence_type
attributes.description: The category of aviation licence. ATPL (Airline Transport Pilot Licence), CPL (Commercial Pilot Licence), MPL (Multi-crew Pilot Licence), cabin crew attestation, flight engineer, or flight navigator.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to this licence record.

attributes.name: ratings_held
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ratings and endorsements held on this licence (e.g., instrument rating, multi-engine, type ratings). This is a summary field; detailed type ratings are tracked in the qualification product.

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: The date on which the licence was last renewed. Null if the licence has never been renewed since original issue.

attributes.name: restrictions
attributes.description: Free-text description of any restrictions or limitations placed on the licence by the issuing authority (e.g., 'Valid only with corrective lenses', 'VFR only', 'Co-pilot only').

attributes.name: revocation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the licence was permanently revoked by the issuing authority. Null if the licence has never been revoked.

attributes.name: revocation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for licence revocation (e.g., serious safety violation, fraud, criminal conviction).

attributes.name: suspension_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which a suspension of the licence is scheduled to end or was lifted. Null if currently suspended with no defined end date.

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for licence suspension (e.g., medical disqualification, regulatory violation, administrative hold).

attributes.name: suspension_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which a suspension of the licence became effective. Null if the licence has never been suspended.

attributes.name: total_flight_hours_at_issue
attributes.description: The total flight hours logged by the crew member at the time the licence was issued. Captured for historical record and regulatory audit.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this licence record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the licence was last verified with the issuing authority.

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Status of the licence verification process with the issuing authority. Verified means the airline has confirmed authenticity with the regulator.

Used for crew availability planning, absence pattern monitoring, and collective agreement compliance.

attributes.name: previous_absence_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the previous absence record if this absence is a recurrence or continuation. Nullable if this is the first occurrence.

attributes.name: reporting_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Absences are reported and managed at crew's assigned station for operational impact assessment, replacement crew sourcing, and station-level crew availability tracking. Critical for daily operations c

attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the absence record: pending approval, approved, rejected, active (ongoing), completed, or cancelled.

attributes.name: absence_type
attributes.description: Classification of the absence reason: sick leave, maternity/paternity leave, compassionate leave, suspension, administrative leave, or unplanned absence. attributes.description: The number of scheduled duty periods impacted by this absence, requiring roster adjustments or crew reassignments.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp

attributes.name: pay_status

attributes.name: replacement_required_flag

attributes.name: return_to_duty_date

domains.name: fleet
domains.description: Single source of truth for aircraft and fleet asset master data including aircraft registration, tail numbers, ICAO/IATA type designators, configuration (cabin layout, seat maps), seating capacity, ownership (owned, wet lease, dry lease, ACMI), APU details, ETOPS certification status, MEL applicability, utilization, block hours, cycles, and fleet planning. products.name: aircraft
products.description: Core master record for every physical aircraft asset in the airline's fleet — the Single Source of Truth for aircraft identity referenced by all operational domains. Captures tail number (registration mark), ICAO/IATA type designator, MSN (Manufacturer Serial Number), line number, aircraft family and variant, current operational status (active, stored, parked, retired, wet-lease-out), ownership category (owned, finance-lease, dry-lease, wet-lease-in, ACMI), lessor/owner reference, delivery date, retirement date, country of registration, certificate of registration number, certificate of airworthiness number, airworthiness category, noise chapter classification, ETOPS certification status and minutes rating, RVSM approval, CAT III ILS approval, and current base station. Following merge of aircraft_registration, also holds regulatory registration details including registering authority, registration date/expiry, and registered owner/operator.
products.reference: ICAO Aircraft Register / IATA Aircraft Type Designator

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the aircraft asset. Primary key for the aircraft master record.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Every aircraft is of a specific type. Aircraft currently denormalizes type-level attributes (icao_type_designator, iata_type_code, aircraft_family, aircraft_variant, manufacturer) that belong in aircr

attributes.name: base_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Aircraft home base assignment drives crew rostering, maintenance scheduling, and fleet deployment planning. Essential for operational planning and cost allocation. Replaces denormalized base_station_c

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: Aircraft leasing is core to airline fleet financing. IFRS16 requires tracking right-of-use assets and lease liabilities by specific aircraft. Finance must link lease contracts to aircraft for lease ac

attributes.name: lessor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.lessor. Business justification: aircraft has denormalized lessor_name (STRING) attribute. For leased aircraft, the lessor is a critical operational reference. The lessor product exists in fleet domain as the authoritative master. Th

attributes.name: airworthiness_category
attributes.description: The category of airworthiness certificate issued. Standard = normal commercial operations; Restricted = limited operations; Limited = special purpose; Experimental = testing; Provisional = pre-certification.

attributes.name: apu_manufacturer
attributes.description: The manufacturer of the Auxiliary Power Unit installed on the aircraft (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney, Hamilton Sundstrand).

attributes.name: apu_model
attributes.description: The specific model designation of the Auxiliary Power Unit installed on the aircraft.

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_code
attributes.description: Internal code identifying the specific cabin layout and seat map configuration installed on this aircraft (e.g., 2-class, 3-class, high-density). Links to detailed seat map reference data.

attributes.name: cat_iii_ils_approved
attributes.business_glossary_term: Category III Instrument Landing System (CAT III ILS) Approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft is equipped and certified for CAT III ILS precision approaches in very low visibility conditions (decision height below 100 feet or no decision height).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 10 Volume I - Radio Navigation Aids

attributes.name: certificate_of_airworthiness_number
attributes.description: The unique certificate number issued by the civil aviation authority certifying that the aircraft meets all safety and airworthiness standards for flight operations.

attributes.name: certificate_of_registration_number
attributes.description: The unique certificate number issued by the civil aviation authority proving legal registration of the aircraft.

attributes.name: country_of_registration
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO country code of the nation where the aircraft is registered (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines regulatory jurisdiction.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this aircraft master record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: delivery_date
attributes.description: The date the aircraft was delivered from the manufacturer to the original customer or the date it entered the current operator's fleet.

attributes.name: etops_certified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft holds ETOPS certification allowing extended-range operations over water or remote areas beyond single-engine diversion time limits.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121 Appendix P

attributes.name: etops_minutes_rating
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Minutes Rating
attributes.description: The maximum diversion time in minutes that the aircraft is certified to fly from the nearest suitable airport under ETOPS rules (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330 minutes). Null if not ETOPS certified.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121 Appendix P

attributes.name: line_number
attributes.description: The sequential production line number assigned by the manufacturer indicating the order in which this aircraft was built within its type series.

attributes.name: mel_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Minimum Equipment List is applicable to this aircraft, allowing dispatch with certain non-critical equipment inoperative under controlled conditions.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121.628

attributes.name: msn
attributes.description: The unique serial number assigned by the aircraft manufacturer at the time of production. Permanent identifier that never changes regardless of ownership or registration.

attributes.name: noise_chapter
attributes.description: The ICAO noise certification standard chapter that the aircraft meets. Chapter 4 is the most stringent current standard. Determines airport access and noise restrictions.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 Volume I - Aircraft Noise

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the aircraft. Active = in revenue service; Stored = long-term storage; Parked = temporary non-operation; Maintenance = undergoing MRO; Retired = permanently withdrawn; Wet_lease_out = leased to another carrier with crew; AOG = Aircraft on Ground (unscheduled maintenance). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|stored|parked|maintenance|retired|wet_lease_out|aog — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ownership_category
attributes.description: The legal and financial ownership structure of the aircraft. Owned = airline owns outright; Finance_lease = capital lease with purchase option; Operating_lease = rental without ownership transfer; Dry_lease = aircraft only; Wet_lease_in = aircraft with crew from lessor; ACMI = Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance lease.
attributes.references: IFRS 16 Leases, IATA Lease Classification Standards

attributes.name: registered_operator
attributes.description: The airline or operator name registered with the civil aviation authority as the entity authorized to operate this aircraft.

attributes.name: registered_owner
attributes.description: The legal entity name appearing on the certificate of registration as the registered owner of the aircraft. May differ from operator for leased aircraft.

attributes.name: registration_authority
attributes.description: The name of the civil aviation authority that issued the certificate of registration (e.g., FAA, EASA, CAAC, Transport Canada).

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date the current certificate of registration was issued by the civil aviation authority.

attributes.name: registration_expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiration date of the current certificate of registration. Aircraft must be re-registered before this date to maintain legal operating authority.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: The date the aircraft was permanently withdrawn from service and retired from the fleet. Null for active aircraft.

attributes.name: rvsm_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft is approved for RVSM operations allowing flight in airspace between FL290 and FL410 with 1,000-foot vertical separation.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9574 - Manual on Implementation of RVSM

attributes.name: seating_capacity_business
attributes.description: The number of seats in the business class cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have business class configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_economy
attributes.description: The number of seats in the economy class cabin.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_first
attributes.description: The number of seats in the first class cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have first class configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_premium_economy
attributes.description: The number of seats in the premium economy cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have premium economy configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_total
attributes.description: The total number of passenger seats installed on the aircraft across all cabin classes. Used for load factor and capacity planning calculations.

attributes.name: tail_number
attributes.description: The official registration mark painted on the aircraft tail, serving as the globally unique identifier for the physical aircraft asset. Also known as registration mark or tail sign.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: total_block_hours
attributes.description: Cumulative total block hours (gate-to-gate flight time) accumulated by the aircraft since delivery. Critical metric for maintenance planning and asset valuation.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Task Force Standards

attributes.name: total_cycles
attributes.description: Cumulative total number of flight cycles (takeoff and landing pairs) accumulated by the aircraft since delivery. Key metric for fatigue life and maintenance interval tracking.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Task Force Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this aircraft master record was last modified in the system.

products.name: aircraft_type
products.description: Reference master for ICAO/IATA aircraft type designators covering all aircraft families and variants operated or planned. Stores ICAO type code, IATA type code, manufacturer name, aircraft family (e.g. B737, A320), variant (e.g. B737-800, A320neo), engine count, engine type (turbofan, turboprop), wake turbulence category (L/M/H/J), maximum certified passenger capacity, maximum structural payload (kg), maximum takeoff weight (MTOW), maximum landing weight (MLW), maximum zero-fuel weight (MZFW), typical range (nm), typical cruise speed (Mach), wingspan (m), fuselage width category (narrowbody/widebody), ETOPS baseline capability, and whether the type is currently in the airline's fleet.
products.reference: ICAO Doc 8643 Aircraft Type Designators

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the aircraft type record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_family
attributes.description: High-level aircraft family grouping (e.g., B737, A320, B777, A350, E190) used for fleet planning and commonality analysis.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the aircraft type in the airline's context: active (currently operated), retired (formerly operated), planned (future fleet addition), reference (not operated, maintained for codeshare/interline/industry reference).

attributes.name: aircraft_variant
attributes.description: Specific aircraft variant within the family including generation and configuration details (e.g., B737-800, A320neo, B777-300ER, A350-900, E190-E2).

attributes.name: apu_manufacturer
attributes.description: Manufacturer of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney Canada, Hamilton Sundstrand).

attributes.name: apu_model
attributes.description: Model designation of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) installed on this aircraft type (e.g., APS3200, GTCP331-500). Used for maintenance planning and ground operations.

attributes.name: cargo_volume_m3
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cargo Hold Volume in Cubic Meters
attributes.description: Total cargo hold volume in cubic meters. Used for cargo revenue planning and ULD capacity analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aircraft type record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: emissions_standard
attributes.description: ICAO engine emissions standard (e.g., CAEP/6, CAEP/8, CAEP/10) indicating compliance level for NOx, CO, HC, and smoke. Used for CORSIA reporting and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 - Environmental Protection, Volume II

attributes.name: engine_count
attributes.description: Number of engines installed on the aircraft type (typically 2, 3, or 4 for commercial jets; 2 for turboprops).

attributes.name: engine_model
attributes.description: Specific engine model and manufacturer (e.g., CFM56-7B, PW1100G-JM, GE90-115B, Trent XWB) used for maintenance planning and fuel efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: engine_type
attributes.description: Propulsion system type installed on the aircraft (turbofan for modern jets, turboprop for regional aircraft, turbojet for older jets, piston for small aircraft).

attributes.name: etops_baseline_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Baseline Minutes
attributes.description: Baseline ETOPS certification in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 330, 370) indicating how far the aircraft can fly from the nearest suitable airport with one engine inoperative. Null for non-ETOPS or multi-engine (3+) aircraft.

attributes.name: etops_certified_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this aircraft type holds ETOPS certification, enabling extended overwater and remote area operations for twin-engine aircraft.

attributes.name: fleet_entry_date
attributes.description: Date when this aircraft type first entered the airline's operating fleet. Null if not yet in fleet or planned only.

attributes.name: fleet_exit_date
attributes.description: Date when this aircraft type was retired from the airline's operating fleet. Null if still active or never operated.

attributes.name: fuel_capacity_liters
attributes.description: Total usable fuel capacity in liters. Critical for range calculation, fuel uplift planning, and operational cost analysis.

attributes.name: fuselage_length_m
attributes.description: Overall length of the aircraft fuselage in meters. Impacts gate compatibility and ground handling requirements.

attributes.name: fuselage_width_category
attributes.description: Classification of aircraft by fuselage width: narrowbody (single-aisle, e.g., A320, B737), widebody (twin-aisle, e.g., A350, B777), regional (smaller single-aisle, e.g., E190, CRJ).

attributes.name: iata_type_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Type Code
attributes.description: Three-character IATA aircraft type code used in reservation systems, schedules, and commercial documentation (e.g., 738 for Boeing 737-800, 32Q for Airbus A321neo).

attributes.name: icao_type_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Type Code
attributes.description: Four-character ICAO aircraft type designator used globally for flight planning, ATC communication, and operational documentation (e.g., B738 for Boeing 737-800, A20N for Airbus A320neo).

attributes.name: in_fleet_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this aircraft type is currently operated in the airline's fleet (true) or is a reference type for codeshare, interline, or future planning (false).

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the aircraft manufacturer (e.g., Boeing, Airbus, Embraer, Bombardier, ATR).

attributes.name: max_passenger_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of passenger seats that can be installed per the aircraft type certificate, regardless of airline-specific configuration. Used for regulatory compliance and emergency planning.
attributes.references: FAA Type Certificate Data Sheet / EASA Type Certificate

attributes.name: max_range_nm
attributes.description: Maximum certified range in nautical miles with maximum fuel and reduced payload. Defines the aircraft's absolute capability for ultra-long-haul operations.

attributes.name: max_structural_payload_kg
attributes.description: Maximum weight of passengers, cargo, and baggage that can be carried, limited by structural design. Critical for load planning and revenue optimization.

attributes.name: mel_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Minimum Equipment List (MEL) is applicable to this aircraft type, allowing dispatch with certain non-critical equipment inoperative under specific conditions.

attributes.name: mlw_kg
attributes.description: Maximum certified weight at which the aircraft is permitted to land. Determines whether fuel jettison is required in emergency return scenarios.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aircraft type record was last modified.

attributes.name: mtow_kg
attributes.description: Maximum certified weight at which the aircraft is permitted to take off. Determines runway length requirements, fuel capacity, and payload trade-offs.

attributes.name: mzfw_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Zero Fuel Weight (MZFW) in Kilograms
attributes.description: Maximum permitted weight of the aircraft and its contents (excluding usable fuel). Limits payload when fuel load is high. Critical for load planning.

attributes.name: noise_chapter
attributes.description: ICAO Annex 16 noise certification chapter (Chapter 2, 3, 4, or 14). Chapter 4 and 14 represent the latest, quietest standards. Critical for airport slot eligibility and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 - Environmental Protection, Volume I

attributes.name: typical_block_fuel_per_hour_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Typical Block Fuel Consumption per Hour (Kilograms)
attributes.description: Average fuel burn per block hour in kilograms under typical operating conditions. Used for CASK calculation, route profitability analysis, and fuel budgeting.
attributes.references: Manufacturer Performance Data / Internal Operations Analysis

attributes.name: typical_cruise_speed_mach
attributes.description: Typical cruise speed expressed as Mach number (e.g., 0.78, 0.82, 0.85). Used for flight planning, schedule optimization, and block time calculation.

attributes.name: typical_range_nm
attributes.description: Typical operational range in nautical miles with standard passenger load and reserves. Used for route network planning and aircraft assignment.

attributes.name: wake_turbulence_category
attributes.description: ICAO wake turbulence category based on maximum takeoff weight: L (Light, <7000kg), M (Medium, 7000-136000kg), H (Heavy, >136000kg), J (Super, A380 only). Critical for ATC separation standards.

attributes.name: wingspan_m
attributes.description: Aircraft wingspan in meters. Determines gate compatibility, taxiway clearance requirements, and ICAO aerodrome reference code.

products.name: cabin_configuration
products.description: Defines the cabin layout and seating configuration installed on a specific aircraft. Each record represents a named configuration version (e.g. 'B738-CFG-A') linked to an aircraft or aircraft type. Captures total seat count, number of cabin classes (e.g. First, Business, Premium Economy, Economy), seat pitch by class, seat width by class, lie-flat availability, in-flight entertainment (IFE) system type, Wi-Fi availability, galley count, lavatory count, door count, overwing exit count, configuration effective date, and configuration retirement date. Supports revenue management seat inventory and passenger service.
products.reference: IATA SSIM Cabin Configuration / Aircraft Seat Map

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the cabin configuration record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific aircraft tail number to which this cabin configuration is installed.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft type (e.g., B738, A320) for which this configuration is designed. Used when configuration applies to a fleet type rather than a single tail.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats in the Business Class cabin. Zero if Business Class is not offered in this configuration.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: Average seat pitch in Business Class, measured in inches. Null if Business Class is not offered.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_width_inches
attributes.description: Average seat width in Business Class, measured in inches. Null if Business Class is not offered.

attributes.name: cabin_class_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct cabin classes in this configuration (e.g., 1 for all-economy, 2 for business and economy, 3 for first/business/economy).

attributes.name: configuration_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the cabin configuration version (e.g., B738-CFG-A, A320-Y180). Used for operational reference and inventory management.

attributes.name: configuration_name
