attributes.description: Timestamp when this station record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this station record was last modified, used for change tracking and data synchronization.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, restrictions, or special handling requirements specific to this station.

attributes.name: slot_coordinated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the airport is slot-coordinated, requiring advance allocation of takeoff and landing slots. True if slot-coordinated, false otherwise.

attributes.name: slot_coordinator_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the slot coordination authority responsible for allocating slots at this airport, if slot-coordinated.

attributes.name: station_name
attributes.description: Official name of the airline operating station, typically matching the airport name or city served.

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the station location, used for flight scheduling and operational coordination.

attributes.name: utc_offset_hours
attributes.description: Standard UTC offset in hours for the station location, excluding daylight saving time adjustments.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

domains.name: route
domains.description: Route network planning and schedule design data including origin-destination (O&D) route definitions, hub-and-spoke network topology, city pairs, frequencies, flight numbers, seasonal schedules, slot allocations at constrained airports, bilateral agreements, codeshare route agreements, ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) capacity planning, and network performance KPIs (OTP, load factor by route). Aligns with Jeppesen scheduling.

products.name: city_pair
products.description: Master definition of an origin-destination (O&D) city pair — the fundamental commercial unit of the airline route network. Captures origin and destination airport/city codes, directionality (one-way vs bidirectional), great circle distance, scheduled distance, IATA region pairing (e.g., TC1-TC2), and market classification (domestic, international, transborder). Serves as the SSOT for all O&D-level demand analysis, RPK aggregation, yield reporting, and market sizing. Referenced by route, market_assessment, and interline agreements.
products.reference: IATA O&D Statistics

attributes.name: city_pair_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the origin-destination city pair. Primary key for the city pair master entity.

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: City pairs define markets between specific stations. Market analysis, demand forecasting, competitive assessment, and bilateral agreement evaluation require direct station links. Role prefix 'origin_'

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is currently active in the airline's route network. Inactive city pairs are retained for historical analysis and potential future reactivation.

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_code
attributes.description: Reference code for the bilateral air service agreement governing this city pair (e.g., US-UK Open Skies, US-Japan bilateral). Determines traffic rights, capacity limits, and operational freedoms.

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is eligible for codeshare operations under existing alliance agreements and regulatory approvals.

attributes.name: competitive_intensity
attributes.description: Market competition classification based on number of carriers serving the city pair: monopoly (single carrier), duopoly (two carriers), oligopoly (3-5 carriers), highly_competitive (6+ carriers).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this city pair record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the destination point of the city pair (e.g., JFK, LAX, LHR).

attributes.name: destination_city_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA city code for the destination metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., LON for LHR/LGW/STN).

attributes.name: destination_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code for the destination country (e.g., USA, GBR, FRA).

attributes.name: destination_iata_region
attributes.description: IATA Traffic Conference region for the destination (TC1=Americas, TC2=Europe/Africa/Middle East, TC3=Asia/Pacific). Used for fare construction and bilateral agreement classification.

attributes.name: directionality
attributes.description: Indicates whether the city pair is defined as one-way (origin to destination only) or bidirectional (both directions treated as same market for analysis).

attributes.name: distance_band
attributes.description: Categorical classification of route length: short_haul (<1500km), medium_haul (1500-4000km), long_haul (4000-8000km), ultra_long_haul (>8000km). Used for fleet assignment, crew planning, and market segmentation.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this city pair definition became effective in the airline's route network. Used for historical analysis and schedule planning.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this city pair definition ceased to be effective (nullable for currently active city pairs). Used for historical analysis and route discontinuation tracking.

attributes.name: etops_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-Range Twin-Engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether ETOPS certification is required for twin-engine aircraft operations on this city pair due to extended overwater or remote routing beyond 60 minutes single-engine diversion time.

attributes.name: great_circle_distance_km
attributes.description: Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in kilometers. Used for ASK and RPK calculations.

attributes.name: great_circle_distance_miles
attributes.description: Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in statute miles. Used for mileage accrual in FFP programs.

attributes.name: hub_spoke_classification
attributes.description: Network topology classification indicating whether the city pair connects two hubs, a hub to a spoke, two spokes, or operates as a point-to-point route outside the hub network.

attributes.name: interline_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers, allowing through-ticketing and baggage transfer.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this city pair record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: market_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the city pair market type: domestic (within same country), international (between different countries), or transborder (specific cross-border markets with special regulatory treatment, e.g., US-Canada).

attributes.name: market_maturity
attributes.description: Lifecycle stage of the city pair market: emerging (new route, low traffic), growth (increasing demand), mature (stable established market), declining (reducing demand).

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time in minutes required for passenger connections at the origin or destination hub when this city pair is part of a connecting itinerary. Used for schedule feasibility and inventory availability.

attributes.name: origin_city_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA city code for the origin metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., NYC for JFK/LGA/EWR).

attributes.name: origin_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code for the origin country (e.g., USA, GBR, FRA).

attributes.name: origin_iata_region
attributes.description: IATA Traffic Conference region for the origin (TC1=Americas, TC2=Europe/Africa/Middle East, TC3=Asia/Pacific). Used for fare construction and bilateral agreement classification.

attributes.name: scheduled_distance_km
attributes.description: Actual flown distance based on typical flight routing including airways, ATC routing, and operational constraints. May differ from great circle distance due to airspace restrictions, weather routing, or operational procedures.

attributes.name: seasonal_pattern
attributes.description: Typical seasonal operating pattern for this city pair: year_round (continuous service), summer_only (IATA summer season), winter_only (IATA winter season), peak_season (high-demand periods), shoulder_season (transitional periods).

attributes.name: slot_constrained_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether either the origin or destination airport is slot-controlled under IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (Level 3 airport), requiring allocated takeoff and landing slots.

attributes.name: time_zone_difference_hours
attributes.description: Time difference in hours between origin and destination time zones. Positive values indicate destination is ahead; negative values indicate destination is behind. Used for schedule planning and passenger communication.

attributes.name: traffic_rights_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Traffic Rights Category (Freedoms of the Air)
attributes.description: ICAO freedom of the air classification applicable to this city pair, defining the operational rights granted under bilateral agreements (e.g., third_freedom for outbound, fourth_freedom for inbound, fifth_freedom for beyond rights). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: first_freedom|second_freedom|third_freedom|fourth_freedom|fifth_freedom|sixth_freedom|seventh_freedom|eighth_freedom|ninth_freedom — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: typical_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Average scheduled block time (gate-to-gate time) in minutes for flights operating this city pair, including taxi time. Used for crew scheduling, aircraft utilization planning, and schedule design.

attributes.name: typical_flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Average airborne flight time in minutes for this city pair, excluding taxi time. Used for fuel planning and flight operations analysis.

products.name: route
products.description: Master record for a defined airline route between an origin and destination airport pair, representing the authoritative network topology entity. Captures route code, origin and destination IATA airport codes, route type (hub-to-hub, hub-to-spoke, spoke-to-spoke, point-to-point), service type (passenger, cargo, mixed), route status (active, suspended, planned, discontinued), inaugural date, suspension date, and applicable bilateral air service agreement reference. Aligns with Jeppesen NetLine/Sched route master.
products.reference: IATA Route Network Definition

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the airline route. Primary key for the route master record.

attributes.name: city_pair_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.city_pair. Business justification: Route operates on a specific origin-destination city pair. Currently route has origin_airport_code and destination_airport_code as separate strings. Adding city_pair_id FK normalizes this relationship

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Routes are operated under a specific legal operating entity (company code) for IFRS P&L attribution, AOC compliance reporting, and route profitability statements. Aviation finance teams require route-

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Routes are primary cost objects in airline network planning. Direct operating costs (crew, fuel, maintenance) are allocated to cost centres by route for CASK calculation, route P&L reporting, and netw

attributes.name: destination_station_id
attributes.description: FK to airport.station

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Routes operate between origin and destination stations. Network planning, slot coordination, bilateral rights validation, and operational readiness all require direct station references. Role prefix '

attributes.name: authority_type
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the route: domestic (within single country), international (between countries), or cabotage (domestic service by foreign carrier, typically restricted).

attributes.name: average_load_factor_percent
attributes.description: Historical average load factor (percentage of seats filled) for this route over the trailing 12 months. Key performance indicator for route profitability.

attributes.name: average_otp_percent
attributes.description: Historical average on-time performance percentage (flights arriving within 15 minutes of scheduled time) for this route over the trailing 12 months.

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard scheduled block time in minutes from gate departure (off-blocks) at origin to gate arrival (on-blocks) at destination. Used for crew scheduling and aircraft utilization planning.

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route is eligible for codeshare agreements with partner airlines (true) or restricted to own-metal operations only (false).

attributes.name: competitive_route_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route faces direct competition from other carriers (true) or is operated exclusively by this airline (false).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this route record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: distance_km
attributes.description: Great circle distance between origin and destination airports in kilometers. Used for ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) and RPK (Revenue Passenger Kilometer) calculations.

attributes.name: distance_miles
attributes.description: Great circle distance between origin and destination airports in statute miles. Used for frequent flyer mileage accrual and US DOT reporting.

attributes.name: etops_rating_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Rating (Minutes)
attributes.description: Required ETOPS rating in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330) for aircraft operating this route. Null if ETOPS not required.

attributes.name: etops_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Required Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route requires ETOPS certification due to extended overwater or remote area operations beyond 60 minutes single-engine diversion time.

attributes.name: flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard airborne flight time in minutes from wheels-up at origin to wheels-down at destination, excluding taxi time.

attributes.name: inaugural_date
attributes.description: Date when the route was first launched and entered commercial service.

attributes.name: interline_eligible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route participates in interline ticketing agreements (true), allowing through-ticketing with other carriers, or is restricted (false).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this route record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: number_of_competitors
attributes.description: Count of other airlines operating direct service on this origin-destination pair. Zero indicates monopoly route.

attributes.name: operating_season
attributes.description: Season during which the route operates: year-round (all seasons), summer-only (IATA summer schedule), or winter-only (IATA winter schedule).

attributes.name: planned_launch_date
attributes.description: Expected date for route launch for routes in planned status. Null for active or discontinued routes.

attributes.name: profitability_tier
attributes.description: Internal classification of route profitability: tier_1 (highest margin), tier_2 (above average), tier_3 (break-even), tier_4 (loss-making). Used for strategic network decisions.

attributes.name: route_code
attributes.description: Six-character alphanumeric code representing the origin-destination pair (e.g., JFKLHR for New York JFK to London Heathrow). Typically constructed as origin IATA code + destination IATA code.

attributes.name: route_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the route: active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily halted), planned (approved but not yet launched), or discontinued (permanently ceased).

attributes.name: route_type
attributes.description: Classification of the route based on network topology: hub-to-hub (connecting two major hubs), hub-to-spoke (hub to regional destination), spoke-to-spoke (regional to regional), or point-to-point (direct service bypassing hubs).

attributes.name: seasonal_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route operates seasonally (true) or year-round (false). Seasonal routes typically align with IATA summer/winter schedule seasons.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of service operated on this route: passenger (pax only), cargo (freight only), or mixed (combination of passenger and cargo).

attributes.name: slot_controlled_destination
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the destination airport is slot-controlled (true), requiring allocated takeoff/landing slots, or non-slot-controlled (false).

attributes.name: slot_controlled_origin
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the origin airport is slot-controlled (true), requiring allocated takeoff/landing slots, or non-slot-controlled (false).

attributes.name: suspension_date
attributes.description: Date when the route was suspended or discontinued. Null if route is currently active or planned.

attributes.name: weekly_frequency
attributes.description: Number of scheduled flights per week on this route. Used for capacity planning and network optimization.

products.name: flight_number
products.description: Master record for airline flight number designators assigned to routes, capturing the IATA/ICAO carrier code prefix, numeric flight number, suffix (if applicable), direction (outbound/inbound), operating carrier, marketing carrier (for codeshare), flight number type (operating, codeshare, wetlease), effective date range, and associated route. Serves as the SSOT for flight number lifecycle management and codeshare number assignment. Aligns with Jeppesen scheduling and Amadeus Altéa inventory.
products.reference: IATA Flight Number Standard

attributes.name: flight_number_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the flight number record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Flight numbers are typically assigned with planned aircraft type for schedule publication, GDS distribution, and passenger booking. Linking to aircraft_type enables fleet assignment validation, seat i

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: flight_number currently has operating_carrier_code as STRING. Normalizing to carrier.carrier_id creates proper referential integrity. The operating carrier is the airline that physically operates the

attributes.name: partnership_id
attributes.description: Reference to the codeshare agreement governing this flight number assignment. Null for operating flights. Links to the bilateral codeshare contract between marketing and operating carriers.

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the origin-destination route that this flight number serves. Links to the route master data defining city pairs and network topology.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: flight_number carries a `season_code` STRING attribute that is a denormalized reference to the IATA schedule season. Adding schedule_season_id as a proper FK to schedule_season normalizes this relatio

attributes.name: slot_allocation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the airport slot allocation record for constrained airports. Links to the assigned takeoff/landing time window granted by the airport coordinator or Air Traffic Control (ATC).

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference code or identifier for the bilateral air service agreement between countries that authorizes this route. Governs traffic rights and frequencies under international aviation treaties.
attributes.references: ICAO Policies on Charges for Airports and Air Navigation Services

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled block time in minutes from gate departure (out) to gate arrival (in) for this flight number. Represents the total elapsed time including taxi, flight, and arrival taxi.

attributes.name: carrier_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Carrier Code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline designator code identifying the carrier (e.g., AA for American Airlines, BA for British Airways). Used as prefix for flight numbers.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flight number record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's destination/arrival airport (e.g., LAX, CDG, SIN).

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Directional classification of the flight within the route network: outbound (departing from hub), inbound (arriving at hub), circular (multi-leg routing returning to origin).

attributes.name: distance_km
attributes.description: Great circle distance in kilometers between origin and destination airports. Used for Revenue Passenger Kilometer (RPK) and Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) calculations.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this flight number assignment becomes active and valid for scheduling and reservations. Start of the flight number's lifecycle.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this flight number assignment expires or is discontinued. Null indicates an open-ended assignment. End of the flight number's lifecycle.

attributes.name: etops_certified_indicator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight operates under Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) certification for extended overwater or remote area operations (true) or standard operations (false).

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: Numeric flight number designator (1-4 digits) with optional single-letter suffix. Combined with carrier code forms the complete flight identifier (e.g., 1234, 567A).

attributes.name: flight_number_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the flight number: active (in operational use), inactive (temporarily not scheduled), suspended (operationally blocked), pending (approved but not yet active), retired (permanently discontinued).

attributes.name: flight_number_type
attributes.description: Classification of the flight number based on operational arrangement: operating (airline operates the flight), codeshare (marketing carrier sells seats on another carrier's flight), wetlease (aircraft leased with crew), drylease (aircraft leased without crew), blocked (reserved but not in active use).

attributes.name: flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled airborne flight time in minutes from wheels-off to wheels-on. Excludes ground taxi time.

attributes.name: frequency_pattern
attributes.description: Seven-character string indicating days of operation (1=operates, 0=does not operate) in sequence Monday through Sunday (e.g., 1111100 = Monday-Friday only, 0000011 = weekends only).

attributes.name: full_flight_number
attributes.description: Complete flight number including carrier code and numeric designator (e.g., AA1234, BA567A). This is the externally-known business identifier displayed to passengers and used in reservations.

attributes.name: gds_distribution_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is distributed through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport for travel agency bookings (true) or restricted to direct channels (false).

attributes.name: icao_carrier_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Carrier Code
attributes.description: Three-character ICAO airline designator code for the carrier (e.g., AAL for American Airlines, BAW for British Airways). Used in flight plans and air traffic control communications.

attributes.name: interline_eligible_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers (true) or restricted to online bookings only (false).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flight number record was last updated. Audit trail for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: marketing_carrier_code
attributes.description: IATA code of the airline that markets and sells the flight. For codeshare flights, this is the carrier whose flight number is displayed. For operating flights, this matches the carrier_code.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this flight number record. Supports audit trail and accountability for schedule changes.

attributes.name: network_hub_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight serves a hub airport in the carrier's hub-and-spoke network topology (true) or is a point-to-point spoke route (false).

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's origin/departure airport (e.g., JFK, LHR, DXB).

attributes.name: priority_ranking
attributes.description: Internal priority ranking for this flight number within the carrier's network. Lower numbers indicate higher priority for resource allocation, slot protection, and operational recovery during Irregular Operations (IROP).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, or additional context about this flight number assignment. May include codeshare display rules, seasonal variations, or historical notes.

attributes.name: revenue_management_class
attributes.description: Revenue management classification code used for yield optimization and inventory control strategies. Aligns with Sabre AirVision Revenue Management system classifications.

attributes.name: seasonal_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is assigned on a seasonal basis (true) or year-round (false). Seasonal flights typically operate during peak travel periods (summer, winter holidays).

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of service provided by the flight: passenger (revenue passenger service), cargo (freight only), combi (mixed passenger and cargo), ferry (non-revenue aircraft repositioning), positioning (crew or equipment repositioning).

attributes.name: traffic_rights_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Traffic Rights Category (Freedoms of the Air)
attributes.description: Classification of air traffic rights under the Freedoms of the Air framework (e.g., First Freedom, Second Freedom, Third Freedom, Fourth Freedom, Fifth Freedom, Sixth Freedom, Seventh Freedom, Eighth Freedom, Ninth Freedom). Defines the scope of international route authority.
attributes.references: ICAO Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention)

products.name: schedule_season
products.description: Reference master for IATA scheduling seasons defining the temporal boundaries for all schedule planning, slot coordination, and capacity deployment activities. Captures season code (e.g., S25, W25/26), season type (summer/winter), start and end dates per IATA calendar, schedule submission deadlines (initial, supplementary), slot return deadlines, and IATA Schedules Conference dates. Serves as the mandatory temporal anchor referenced by seasonal_schedule, route_slot_allocation, ask_plan, and route_fleet_assignment.
products.reference: IATA Scheduling Guidelines

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IATA scheduling season record. Primary key.

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: IATA schedule seasons (S/W) directly drive airline budget planning cycles. Finance teams create budget plans aligned to each schedule season for capacity, revenue, and cost forecasting. Aviation plann

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this schedule season record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: daylight_saving_transition_applicable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Daylight Saving Time (DST) Transition Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether daylight saving time transitions occur during this scheduling season, requiring schedule adjustments for affected routes and airports. True if DST transitions occur within the season period.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of calendar days in the scheduling season, calculated from start_date to end_date inclusive. Typically ranges from 180 to 185 days.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the IATA scheduling season when the seasonal schedule expires. Typically the Saturday before the next season starts.

attributes.name: historical_use_it_or_lose_it_threshold_percent
attributes.description: The minimum slot utilization percentage required during this season to retain grandfather rights for the next equivalent season. Typically 80% per IATA WSG, but may vary by jurisdiction (e.g., EU Regulation 95/93). Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 80.00 for 80%).
attributes.references: IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG), EU Regulation 95/93

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference End Date
attributes.description: The end date of the biannual IATA Schedules Conference. Conferences typically last 3-5 days and occur twice per year (spring for winter season, fall for summer season).

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_location
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference Location
attributes.description: The city and country where the IATA Schedules Conference for this season is held (e.g., 'Geneva, Switzerland', 'Singapore').

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference Start Date
attributes.description: The start date of the biannual IATA Schedules Conference where airlines, airports, and slot coordinators meet to coordinate seasonal schedules, negotiate slots, and finalize bilateral agreements.

attributes.name: iata_season_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Season Year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which the season primarily falls or begins, used for grouping and filtering seasons by year (e.g., 2025 for S25 or W25/26).

attributes.name: initial_schedule_submission_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline by which airlines must submit their initial seasonal schedule requests to slot coordinators and Global Distribution Systems (GDS). Typically occurs several months before season start per IATA Schedules Information Standards (SIS).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this schedule season record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: northern_hemisphere_dst_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Northern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) End Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time ends in the northern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in November for North America, last Sunday in October for Europe). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: northern_hemisphere_dst_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Northern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) Start Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time begins in the northern hemisphere during this season (typically second Sunday in March for North America, last Sunday in March for Europe). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional information, special circumstances, or operational notes relevant to this scheduling season (e.g., COVID-19 slot relief measures, exceptional slot waiver periods, regulatory changes).

attributes.name: peak_travel_period_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this season is considered a peak travel period with higher demand and load factors. Summer seasons are typically peak periods for leisure travel in the northern hemisphere.

attributes.name: schedule_season_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheduling season. Planning: season is being prepared and schedules are being submitted. Active: season is currently in effect. Completed: season has ended but data is still operational. Archived: season is historical and closed for reporting only.

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Season Code
attributes.description: IATA standard season code identifying the scheduling period. Format: S25 for Summer 2025, W25/26 for Winter 2025/2026. This is the externally-known business identifier for the season.

attributes.name: season_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the scheduling season (e.g., 'Summer 2025', 'Winter 2025/2026').

attributes.name: season_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scheduling season into IATA-defined periods: summer (typically late March to late October) or winter (typically late October to late March).

attributes.name: slot_coordination_cycle
attributes.description: The IATA slot coordination cycle identifier corresponding to this season, used by slot coordinators at Level 2 and Level 3 airports for capacity management and slot allocation.

attributes.name: slot_return_deadline
attributes.description: The final date by which airlines must return unused or unwanted airport slots to the slot coordinator to avoid use-it-or-lose-it penalties. Critical for slot allocation compliance at Level 3 coordinated airports.

attributes.name: southern_hemisphere_dst_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Southern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) End Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time ends in the southern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in April for Australia). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: southern_hemisphere_dst_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Southern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) Start Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time begins in the southern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in October for Australia). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the IATA scheduling season when the seasonal schedule becomes effective. Typically the last Sunday of March for summer seasons and last Sunday of October for winter seasons.

attributes.name: supplementary_schedule_submission_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline for airlines to submit supplementary or revised schedule changes after the initial submission. Allows for adjustments closer to the season start date.

products.name: seasonal_schedule
products.description: Operational schedule plan for a specific route during an IATA season, defining the planned service pattern including days of operation (DOW mask), departure and arrival times (local and UTC), frequency per week, cabin configuration, planned aircraft type, block time, and schedule status (planned, filed, approved, active, cancelled). Represents the filed schedule submitted to IATA and slot coordinators. Aligns with Jeppesen Flight Planning System seasonal schedule module.
products.reference: IATA Scheduling Guidelines (SSG)

attributes.name: seasonal_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the seasonal schedule record. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Seasonal schedules must reference valid aircraft types to enforce fleet availability constraints, validate seat capacity, verify ETOPS certification for route requirements, and support schedule-to-fle

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Seasonal schedules are the primary unit of airline financial planning — each scheduled operation has an associated budget for revenue, fuel, and crew costs. Direct FK enables budget vs actual variance

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.cabin_configuration. Business justification: Seasonal schedule capacity planning requires the exact cabin configuration to compute available seats by class (ASK, load factor by cabin). seasonal_schedule.aircraft_configuration_code is a denormali

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Airlines with multiple AOC holders must attribute each scheduled operation to the correct legal entity for regulatory reporting and IFRS revenue recognition. seasonal_schedule has operating_carrier_id

attributes.name: cost_centre_id

attributes.name: origin_station_id
