attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.terminal_facility. Business justification: Airlines file terminal preferences with schedule submissions for capacity planning and passenger connectivity. origin_terminal is a denormalized text field; a FK to terminal_facility enables terminal

attributes.name: primary_seasonal_marketing_carrier_id
attributes.description: FK to route.carrier

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route for which this seasonal schedule is defined. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination city pair.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: Seasonal_schedule currently has iata_season_code (STRING) but should reference schedule_season via FK. Every seasonal schedule operates within a defined IATA season. The schedule_season table is the a

attributes.name: slot_allocation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route_slot_allocation. Business justification: seasonal_schedule carries `slot_time_origin` and `slot_time_destination` STRING attributes that represent the allocated slot times at origin and destination airports. These are denormalized copies of

attributes.name: aircraft_owner
attributes.description: Indicates the ownership/lease arrangement for the aircraft planned for this schedule. Values: owned (airline-owned), wet_lease (leased with crew), dry_lease (leased without crew), acmi (Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance lease), charter (chartered from third party).

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule received final approval from all required authorities (slot coordinators, civil aviation authorities, bilateral agreement partners). Nullable if not yet approved.

attributes.name: arrival_time_local
attributes.description: Scheduled arrival time in local time at the destination airport. Format: HH:MM (24-hour). This is the planned gate arrival time (on-blocks time) in the destination airport local timezone. May show next-day arrival if flight crosses midnight.

attributes.name: arrival_time_utc
attributes.description: Scheduled arrival time in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Format: HH:MM (24-hour). Used for operational planning and coordination across time zones.

attributes.name: ask_planned
attributes.description: Planned Available Seat Kilometers for this seasonal schedule. Calculated as total seats multiplied by route distance in kilometers. Key capacity metric for network planning and revenue management.

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled block time in minutes. Block time is the total time from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks), including taxi time at both airports. Used for crew duty calculations and operational planning.

attributes.name: codeshare_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this seasonal schedule is part of a codeshare agreement. True if the flight is operated by one airline but marketed under multiple airline codes. False for solely-operated flights.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: day_change_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates the number of days difference between departure and arrival dates. Values: 0 (same day), 1 (next day), 2 (two days later), -1 (previous day for flights crossing international date line westbound). Used to calculate actual arrival date from departure date.

attributes.name: days_of_operation
attributes.description: Seven-character string representing the days of the week this flight operates. Each position represents a day (Monday through Sunday). Values: 1=operates, 0=does not operate. Example: 1111100 means Monday-Friday only. Also known as DOW (Day of Week) mask.

attributes.name: departure_time_local
attributes.description: Scheduled departure time in local time at the origin airport. Format: HH:MM (24-hour). This is the planned gate departure time (off-blocks time) in the origin airport local timezone.

attributes.name: departure_time_utc
attributes.description: Scheduled departure time in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Format: HH:MM (24-hour). Used for operational planning and coordination across time zones.

attributes.name: destination_terminal
attributes.description: Terminal identifier at the destination airport where this flight arrives. Used for passenger information and ground operations planning. Format varies by airport (e.g., 1, A, T1, North).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The first date on which this seasonal schedule becomes effective. Marks the start of the schedule validity period within the IATA season.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The last date on which this seasonal schedule is effective. Marks the end of the schedule validity period within the IATA season. Nullable for open-ended schedules.

attributes.name: filed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule was officially filed with IATA and relevant slot coordinators. Represents the submission timestamp for regulatory and coordination purposes.

attributes.name: frequency_per_week
attributes.description: The number of times this flight operates per week during the seasonal schedule period. Derived from the days_of_operation mask. Range: 0-7.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: meal_service_code
attributes.description: IATA meal service code indicating the type of meal service planned for this flight. Common values: B=Breakfast, L=Lunch, D=Dinner, S=Snack, M=Meal (unspecified), N=No meal service. Used for catering planning and passenger information.
attributes.references: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or operational comments related to this seasonal schedule. May include information about seasonal variations, special events, or coordination notes.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the seasonal schedule. Values: planned (initial planning stage), filed (submitted to IATA and slot coordinators), approved (regulatory and slot approval received), active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily not operating), cancelled (permanently removed from schedule).

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: IATA service type code indicating the nature of the flight service. Values: J=Passenger Jet, F=Cargo, C=Charter, P=Positioning/Ferry. Passenger scheduled services typically use J.

attributes.name: total_seats
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats available on the planned aircraft configuration for this seasonal schedule. Used for capacity planning and ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) calculations.

attributes.name: traffic_restriction_code
attributes.description: IATA traffic restriction code indicating any limitations on passenger carriage. Examples: G=Government approval required, X=Technical stop (no traffic rights), T=Technical stop with traffic rights. Blank if no restrictions apply.

products.name: slot_allocation
products.description: Airport slot allocation record for a specific route and season at a slot-coordinated (Level 2 or Level 3) airport. Captures slot coordinator reference number, allocated departure or arrival time, slot type (historical grandfather, new entrant, pool), slot series (full season or partial), days of operation, aircraft type restriction, slot status (requested, allocated, confirmed, returned, swapped), and IATA slot coordination conference reference. Critical for constrained airports (LHR, JFK, CDG, NRT). Aligns with IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG).
products.reference: IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: slot_allocation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the airport slot allocation record. Primary key for the route slot allocation entity.

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Airport slot costs are significant operating expenses at slot-constrained airports (LHR, JFK, NRT). Airlines allocate slot acquisition, holding, and opportunity costs to route cost centres for route p

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route for which this slot is allocated. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination city pair and service characteristics.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: Route_slot_allocation currently has slot_season_code (STRING) but should reference schedule_season via FK. Slot allocations are granted for specific IATA seasons. The schedule_season table contains th

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Slot allocations are station-specific regulatory permissions. Slot utilization tracking, coordinator coordination, historic rights validation, and compliance reporting require direct station link. No

attributes.name: aircraft_size_category
attributes.description: General aircraft size category restriction for the slot. Used when specific type restrictions are not applied but size-based capacity management is in effect.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_restriction
attributes.description: ICAO aircraft type code restriction for this slot allocation (e.g., B738, A320, B77W). Some slots at noise-sensitive or capacity-constrained airports may be restricted to specific aircraft types or size categories. Null if no restriction applies.
attributes.references: ICAO Aircraft Type Designators, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: allocated_time
attributes.description: The specific time allocated for the departure or arrival movement in local airport time (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock). This is the coordinated time window the airline must operate within.

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the bilateral air service agreement between countries that governs traffic rights and slot access for this route. Relevant for international routes where slot allocation must comply with bilateral treaty provisions.
attributes.references: ICAO Bilateral Air Service Agreements, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this slot allocation record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for slot coordination data lineage.

attributes.name: days_of_operation
attributes.description: Days of the week on which this slot is allocated, represented as a string of digits where 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, 4=Thursday, 5=Friday, 6=Saturday, 7=Sunday. For example, '1357' means Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Sunday. Empty or '1234567' indicates daily operation.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The first date on which this slot allocation becomes effective. For full season slots, this is typically the season start date. For partial season slots, this is the first date of the allocated period.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The last date on which this slot allocation is effective. For full season slots, this is typically the season end date. For partial season slots, this is the last date of the allocated period.

attributes.name: environmental_restriction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is subject to environmental restrictions such as noise abatement procedures, curfew limitations, or emissions-based access rules. True if environmental constraints apply to the slot usage.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 (Environmental Protection), IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: historical_precedence_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot carries historical precedence (grandfather rights) for the airline. True if the airline has operated this slot in previous equivalent seasons and is entitled to priority retention under IATA use-it-or-lose-it rules (80% usage threshold).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this slot allocation record was last updated. Tracks changes to slot status, times, or other allocation parameters throughout the coordination lifecycle.

attributes.name: slot_allocation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the slot coordinator officially allocated this slot to the airline. Marks the transition from requested to allocated status.

attributes.name: slot_cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Reason for cancellation of the slot allocation by the coordinator or airline. Populated when slot_status is 'cancelled'. May include regulatory changes, airport capacity reductions, or airline non-compliance with usage requirements.

attributes.name: slot_conference_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA slot coordination conference where this slot was discussed or allocated (e.g., IATA Slot Conference Worldwide, Regional Slot Conference). IATA holds biannual slot conferences where airlines and coordinators negotiate slot allocations.

attributes.name: slot_confirmation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the airline confirmed acceptance and intention to use the allocated slot. Required by IATA WSG to retain slot rights for future seasons.

attributes.name: slot_coordination_level
attributes.description: IATA coordination level of the airport for this slot. Level 1 (non-coordinated): no slot coordination required; Level 2 (schedule-facilitated): voluntary schedule coordination; Level 3 (fully coordinated): mandatory slot allocation by coordinator. Only Level 2 and Level 3 airports issue formal slot allocations.

attributes.name: slot_coordinator_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number assigned by the airport slot coordinator to this slot allocation. Used for official correspondence and slot coordination activities.

attributes.name: slot_movement_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is for an arrival or departure movement at the coordinated airport.

attributes.name: slot_priority_score
attributes.description: Numeric score assigned by the slot coordinator to prioritize this slot request relative to competing requests. Higher scores indicate higher priority. Factors include historical precedence, new entrant status, network connectivity, and public interest considerations.

attributes.name: slot_request_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the airline submitted the slot request to the coordinator. Used to establish priority in slot allocation processes where multiple carriers request the same time.

attributes.name: slot_return_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for returning the slot to the coordinator pool. Populated when slot_status is 'returned'. Common reasons include route discontinuation, schedule optimization, fleet changes, or commercial underperformance.

attributes.name: slot_series_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the slot allocation covers the full IATA season, a partial period within the season, or a single date. Full season slots run for the entire summer or winter season; partial season slots cover a subset of dates.

attributes.name: slot_status
attributes.description: Current status of the slot allocation in the coordination lifecycle. Requested: airline has submitted a slot request; Allocated: coordinator has provisionally allocated the slot; Confirmed: airline has confirmed acceptance and usage; Returned: airline has returned the slot to the pool; Swapped: slot has been exchanged with another carrier; Cancelled: slot allocation has been cancelled.

attributes.name: slot_swap_partner_airline_code
attributes.description: IATA airline code of the partner airline involved in a slot swap transaction. Populated only when slot_status is 'swapped'. Slot swaps allow airlines to exchange slots to optimize their network schedules.
attributes.references: IATA Airline Codes, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: slot_swap_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number for the slot swap transaction, assigned by the slot coordinator. Links this slot allocation to the corresponding swapped slot record.

attributes.name: slot_tolerance_minutes
attributes.description: Number of minutes before or after the allocated time within which the flight operation is considered compliant with the slot. Typically -5 to +10 minutes for departures and -10 to +5 minutes for arrivals, but varies by airport coordinator policy.

attributes.name: slot_type
attributes.description: Classification of the slot allocation type. Historical grandfather slots are held by airlines with historic precedence; new entrant slots are reserved for new carriers; pool slots are available for general allocation; ad hoc slots are one-time allocations; emergency slots are for irregular operations.

attributes.name: slot_usage_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of allocated slot times that were actually used by the airline during the season. IATA WSG requires 80% usage to retain historical rights. Calculated as (flights operated within slot tolerance / total allocated slot occurrences) * 100.

attributes.name: terminal_restriction
attributes.description: Specific terminal designation at the airport where this slot must be used (e.g., Terminal 1, Terminal 5, Concourse B). Some airports allocate slots with terminal restrictions due to capacity or operational constraints.

products.name: partnership
products.description: Master record for all carrier-to-carrier commercial partnership arrangements at the route level, encompassing codeshare agreements, interline ticketing agreements, special prorate agreements (SPAs), and joint venture arrangements. Captures partner carrier IATA code, agreement type (codeshare free-flow, codeshare block-space, standard interline, SPA, through-check-in, joint venture), applicable routes or O&D pairs, revenue sharing basis (prorate, block-space, revenue-share pool), cabin class availability, baggage through-check eligibility, e-ticket interline capability, effective date, expiry date, and agreement status. Serves as the SSOT for all route-level partnership data enabling multi-carrier itinerary construction, codeshare flight number assignment, and interline revenue settlement.
products.reference: IATA Interline Traffic Agreements

attributes.name: partnership_id
attributes.description: Primary key for partnership

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Codeshare partnerships have revenue-sharing and prorate settlements tracked by cost centres. Airlines allocate codeshare revenue, commission expenses, and settlement costs to route cost centres for pa

attributes.name: partnership_operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: FK to route.carrier

attributes.name: partnership_partner_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: partnership currently has partner_carrier_iata_code as STRING. Normalizing to carrier.carrier_id establishes proper FK to the partner carrier in the codeshare/interline partnership. The partner_carrie

attributes.name: route_codeshare_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the route partnership agreement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Route_partnership (codeshare/partnership agreements) currently has origin_airport_iata_code and destination_airport_iata_code as separate strings. These define a route. Adding route_id FK links the pa

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for this partnership agreement, used in contracts and commercial correspondence.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the partnership agreement: draft (under negotiation), pending_approval (awaiting executive sign-off), active (in force), suspended (temporarily inactive), terminated (ended before expiry), or expired (reached natural end date).

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the commercial partnership arrangement: codeshare free-flow (marketing carrier sells seats on operating carrier inventory), codeshare block-space (marketing carrier purchases block of seats), standard interline (ticketing and baggage transfer agreement), special prorate agreement (SPA - negotiated revenue split), through-check-in (baggage handling only), or joint venture (revenue and cost sharing alliance).

attributes.name: antitrust_immunity_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the partnership (typically joint venture) has been granted antitrust immunity by regulatory authorities, allowing revenue and capacity coordination.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this partnership agreement received final executive approval.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the executive or commercial manager who approved this partnership agreement.

attributes.name: auto_renewal_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the partnership agreement automatically renews for an additional term upon expiry unless either party provides notice of termination.

attributes.name: baggage_through_check_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers on interline itineraries under this agreement are eligible for baggage through-check (baggage checked to final destination without re-check at transfer point).

attributes.name: block_space_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats purchased by the marketing carrier under a block-space codeshare agreement. Null if not a block-space agreement.

attributes.name: cabin_class_availability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of cabin classes (e.g., F, J, W, Y) for which this partnership agreement applies. Null if applies to all classes.

attributes.name: codeshare_flight_number_range_end
attributes.description: Ending flight number in the range allocated to the marketing carrier for codeshare flights under this agreement. Null if not a codeshare agreement.

attributes.name: codeshare_flight_number_range_start
attributes.description: Starting flight number in the range allocated to the marketing carrier for codeshare flights under this agreement. Null if not a codeshare agreement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this partnership agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the partnership agreement becomes active and binding.

attributes.name: eticket_interline_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether electronic ticketing is supported for interline itineraries under this agreement (both carriers must support e-ticket interline).

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the partnership agreement expires or is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended agreements.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_accrual_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers can accrue frequent flyer miles/points on the partner carrier when traveling on codeshare or interline flights under this agreement.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_redemption_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers can redeem frequent flyer miles/points for award travel on the partner carrier under this agreement.

attributes.name: gds_distribution_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether codeshare flights under this agreement are distributed through Global Distribution Systems (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) for travel agent booking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this partnership agreement record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time in minutes required for passenger connections between the partner carriers under this agreement, used for interline itinerary construction.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special terms, or operational notes related to this partnership agreement.

attributes.name: notice_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days advance notice required by either party to terminate the partnership agreement.

attributes.name: prorate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of ticket revenue allocated to the partner carrier under prorate revenue sharing. Null if revenue_sharing_basis is not prorate.

attributes.name: revenue_sharing_basis
attributes.description: Method by which revenue is allocated between partner carriers: prorate (IATA standard prorate formula based on mileage), block_space (fixed payment for seat block), revenue_share_pool (joint venture pooling), cost_plus (cost reimbursement plus margin), or fixed_fee (flat payment per flight or period).

attributes.name: route_scope
attributes.description: Geographic scope of the partnership agreement: specific_od_pair (applies to one origin-destination pair), regional_network (applies to routes within a region), or global_network (applies to all routes between the carriers).

attributes.name: settlement_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which revenue settlements between partner carriers are conducted under this agreement.

attributes.name: settlement_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which revenue settlements are processed between partner carriers: weekly, biweekly, monthly, or quarterly.

attributes.name: special_service_request_passthrough
attributes.description: Indicates whether Special Service Requests (meal preferences, wheelchair assistance, etc.) are passed through between carriers for interline passengers under this agreement.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the partnership agreement was terminated, if terminated before the scheduled expiry_date. Null if not terminated early.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the partnership agreement was terminated early, if applicable.

products.name: interline_agreement
products.description: Master record for interline ticketing and traffic agreements between the airline and partner carriers at the route or network level. Captures partner carrier IATA code, agreement type (standard interline, special prorate agreement, through-check-in), applicable O&D pairs, prorate basis (IATA prorate factor, mileage, negotiated), baggage through-check eligibility, e-ticket interline capability, BSP/ARC settlement basis, effective date, and agreement status. Enables multi-carrier itinerary construction and revenue settlement.
products.reference: IATA Interline Traffic Agreements (ITA)

attributes.name: interline_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the interline ticketing and traffic agreement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Interline agreements generate prorate revenue and settlement costs tracked by cost centres. Airlines allocate interline revenue, prorate expenses, and BSP/ARC settlement costs to route cost centres fo

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Interline safety events affect agreement terms (baggage liability, IROP reprotection) and partner safety performance evaluation. Required for interline agreement compliance and partner monitoring. Lin

attributes.name: partner_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: interline_agreement has partner_carrier_iata_code as STRING. Normalizing to carrier.carrier_id establishes FK to the partner carrier in the interline ticketing agreement. This connects interline_agree

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: Route_interline_agreement currently has origin_airport_iata_code and destination_airport_iata_code as separate strings. These define a route. Adding route_id FK links the interline agreement to the au

attributes.name: agreement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, restrictions, or operational instructions related to the interline agreement.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interline agreement indicating whether it is active, suspended, terminated, pending approval, expired, or under negotiation.

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interline agreement defining the scope and nature of the partnership (standard interline, special prorate agreement, through check-in, codeshare interline, virtual interline, bilateral prorate).

attributes.name: alliance_membership
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interline agreement is facilitated by membership in a global airline alliance (Star Alliance, oneworld, SkyTeam, Value Alliance) or is a standalone bilateral agreement (none).

attributes.name: baggage_through_check_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether baggage can be checked through to the final destination across both carriers under this interline agreement (True) or must be reclaimed and re-checked (False).

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interline agreement permits codeshare flight operations between the airline and partner carrier (True) or is limited to standard interline ticketing (False).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: e_ticket_interline_capable
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether electronic ticketing (e-ticket) is supported for interline itineraries under this agreement (True) or paper tickets are required (False).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interline agreement becomes binding and operational for ticketing and traffic purposes.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interline agreement expires or terminates. Nullable for open-ended agreements subject to notice-based termination.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_accrual_eligible
attributes.business_glossary_term: Frequent Flyer Program (FFP) Accrual Eligible Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether passengers can accrue frequent flyer miles or points on the partner carrier segments under this interline agreement (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: gds_distribution_enabled
attributes.business_glossary_term: Global Distribution System (GDS) Distribution Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether interline itineraries under this agreement are available for booking through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport (True) or restricted to direct channels (False).

attributes.name: irop_reprotection_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether passengers can be reprotected on the partner carrier in case of irregular operations (IROP) such as delays, cancellations, or missed connections (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline agreement record was last updated or modified in the system.

attributes.name: liability_limit_sdr
attributes.business_glossary_term: Liability Limit in Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
attributes.description: Maximum liability limit per passenger for baggage, delay, or injury claims under the interline agreement, expressed in Special Drawing Rights (SDR) as defined by the Montreal Convention.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum connecting time in minutes required at the transfer point for interline connections under this agreement. Ensures operational feasibility of through-ticketing.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this interline agreement record. Supports audit trail and data governance.

attributes.name: prorate_basis
attributes.description: Method used to allocate revenue between carriers for interline journeys: IATA prorate factor, mileage-based calculation, negotiated fixed split, revenue share percentage, or cost-plus model.

attributes.name: prorate_percentage
attributes.description: Negotiated percentage of total fare allocated to the operating carrier or partner carrier under the prorate agreement. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: route_scope
attributes.description: Defines the geographic or network scope of the interline agreement: network-wide (all routes), specific city pair, regional coverage, hub-and-spoke network, or alliance network.

attributes.name: settlement_basis
attributes.description: Financial settlement mechanism for interline revenue: BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan), ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation), direct billing between carriers, ICH (IATA Clearing House), or bilateral settlement agreement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728 - Billing and Settlement Plan

attributes.name: special_prorate_agreement_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for a Special Prorate Agreement (SPA) filed with IATA or negotiated bilaterally, if applicable. Nullable for standard interline agreements.

attributes.name: ssr_handling_agreement
attributes.description: Defines the level of Special Service Request (SSR) data exchange and handling between carriers: full SSR exchange, limited SSR support, or no SSR exchange.

products.name: performance
products.description: Operational performance record for a route over a defined measurement period (monthly or seasonal), capturing actual vs planned KPIs including OTP (On-Time Performance percentage), load factor (actual passengers / available seats), RPK (Revenue Passenger Kilometers), ASK (Available Seat Kilometers), RASK (Revenue per ASK), CASK (Cost per ASK), yield (revenue per RPK), cancellation rate, diversion rate, and average block time variance. Serves as the route-level operational scorecard. Distinct from flight-level OOOI data owned by the flight domain.
products.reference: IATA Industry Statistics

attributes.name: performance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the route performance measurement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Route performance variance analysis requires linking actuals to budget. Airlines compare actual route performance metrics (revenue, costs, load factor) against budget plans for variance reporting, for

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Route performance measurement requires cost centre attribution for P&L reporting. Airlines track actual route revenue, costs, and profitability by cost centre for management reporting, route performan

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Route performance financials (total_revenue_amount, total_cost_amount, RASK, CASK) must reconcile to GL postings for financial close. Direct FK enables route P&L to GL reconciliation — a mandatory air

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route being measured. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination pair, flight number pattern, and network topology.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA schedule season during which this performance was measured (e.g., Summer 2024, Winter 2023/24). Links to schedule_season for season boundaries and slot coordination context.

attributes.name: ask
attributes.description: The total number of seat-kilometers available for sale on this route. Calculated as sum of (available seats on each flight * flight distance in km). Fundamental capacity metric.
attributes.references: IATA Traffic Statistics, ICAO Statistical Reporting

attributes.name: available_seats_total
attributes.description: The total number of seats available for sale on all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Basis for load factor calculation.

attributes.name: average_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: The mean block time (gate-to-gate elapsed time) for all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Used for schedule planning and crew productivity analysis.

attributes.name: average_delay_minutes
attributes.description: The mean arrival delay in minutes for all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Negative values indicate early arrivals.

attributes.name: block_time_variance_minutes
attributes.description: The difference between average actual block time and scheduled block time. Positive values indicate flights took longer than scheduled; negative values indicate shorter actual times. Used for schedule buffer optimization.

attributes.name: cancellation_rate_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of scheduled flights that were cancelled. Calculated as (flights cancelled / flights scheduled) * 100. Key operational reliability metric.

attributes.name: cask
attributes.description: Cost per unit of capacity. Calculated as (total cost / ASK). Key unit cost metric for route efficiency analysis. Expressed in cost_currency_code per kilometer.

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which total_cost_amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this route performance record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format, Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: diversion_rate_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of operated flights that were diverted. Calculated as (flights diverted / flights operated) * 100. Indicator of weather, ATC, or operational disruption impact.

attributes.name: flights_cancelled_count
attributes.description: The total number of scheduled flights that were cancelled on this route during the measurement period.

attributes.name: flights_diverted_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights that were diverted to an alternate airport on this route during the measurement period.

attributes.name: flights_operated_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights that actually departed on this route during the measurement period. Excludes cancelled flights.

attributes.name: flights_scheduled_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights scheduled to operate on this route during the measurement period, as published in the airline schedule.

attributes.name: grade
attributes.description: Overall qualitative assessment of route performance based on composite scoring of OTP, load factor, yield, and RASK against targets. Used for executive dashboards and network optimization prioritization.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this route performance record was most recently updated. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format, Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: load_factor_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of available seats that were occupied by revenue passengers. Calculated as (passengers carried / available seats) * 100. Core capacity utilization metric.

attributes.name: measurement_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the performance measurement period. Typically the last day of a calendar month or the end of a seasonal period.

attributes.name: measurement_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the performance measurement period. Typically the first day of a calendar month or the start of a seasonal period.

attributes.name: measurement_period_type
attributes.description: The granularity of the performance measurement period. Monthly is most common for operational scorecards; seasonal aligns with IATA schedule seasons; custom supports ad-hoc analysis windows.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text commentary on exceptional performance factors, IROP events, competitive actions, seasonal effects, or other context relevant to interpreting the performance metrics for this period.

attributes.name: otp_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of operated flights that arrived within 15 minutes of scheduled arrival time. Industry-standard KPI for route punctuality. Calculated as (on-time arrivals / flights operated) * 100.
attributes.references: IATA Punctuality Standards, DOT 14 CFR Part 234

attributes.name: passengers_carried_count
attributes.description: The total number of revenue passengers transported on this route during the measurement period. Excludes non-revenue passengers (crew, deadheads, etc.).

attributes.name: rask
attributes.description: Revenue per unit of capacity. Calculated as (total revenue / ASK). Key unit revenue metric for route profitability analysis. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.

attributes.name: revenue_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which total_revenue_amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: rpk
attributes.description: The total number of kilometers flown by revenue passengers on this route. Calculated as sum of (passengers on each flight * flight distance in km). Fundamental traffic volume metric.
attributes.references: IATA Traffic Statistics, ICAO Statistical Reporting

attributes.name: total_cost_amount
attributes.description: The total operating cost allocated to this route during the measurement period, including direct costs (fuel, crew, airport charges) and allocated indirect costs (maintenance, overhead). Used for route profitability analysis.

attributes.name: total_revenue_amount
attributes.description: The total passenger revenue generated on this route during the measurement period, including base fare, fuel surcharges, and ancillary revenue allocated to the route. Excludes cargo revenue.

attributes.name: yield
attributes.description: Revenue per unit of traffic. Calculated as (total revenue / RPK). Measures pricing power and fare realization. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.

products.name: block_time_standard
products.description: Reference master for planned block time standards by route and aircraft type, representing the scheduled gate-to-gate flight time used in schedule construction and crew pairing. Captures route, aircraft type, direction (outbound/inbound), planned block time (minutes), taxi-out time, taxi-in time, airborne time, seasonal adjustment (summer/winter winds), and last review date. Block time standards are the foundation of crew duty time calculations, fuel planning, and OTP measurement.
products.reference: IATA Block Time Standards

attributes.name: block_time_standard_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the block time standard record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Block time standards are aircraft-type-specific (cruise speed, climb/descent performance vary by type). Linking to aircraft_type enables accurate schedule planning, fuel burn estimation, crew duty cal

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Block time standards affect crew and fuel cost allocation by route. Airlines use block time standards to allocate crew duty costs, fuel burn, and aircraft utilization costs to route cost centres for c

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route for which this block time standard applies. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination city pair.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA schedule season for which this block time standard is effective. Links to the schedule season master defining the IATA summer/winter season boundaries.

attributes.name: airborne_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned airborne time in minutes from takeoff (wheels-up) to landing (wheels-down). Represents the actual flight time in the air, excluding ground operations.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this block time standard was formally approved for operational use. Represents the governance checkpoint ensuring block time standards meet safety, efficiency, and reliability requirements.

attributes.name: atc_delay_factor_minutes
attributes.description: Expected ATC delay factor in minutes based on historical congestion patterns at origin and destination airports, en-route airspace constraints, and time-of-day traffic density.

attributes.name: block_time_standard_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the block time standard. Active standards are used for schedule construction; inactive standards are historical; under_review standards are being validated; superseded standards have been replaced by newer versions.

attributes.name: contingency_buffer_minutes
attributes.description: Additional buffer time in minutes added to the planned block time to account for operational variability, ATC delays, weather, and other uncertainties. Used to improve schedule reliability and OTP performance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this block time standard record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: crew_duty_time_minutes
attributes.description: Block time used for crew duty time and flight time limitation calculations. May include additional time for pre-flight briefing, post-flight duties, and regulatory compliance. Foundation for crew pairing and rostering.
attributes.references: FAA 14 CFR Part 117, EASA Flight Time Limitations

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or methodology used to derive this block time standard. Examples include historical flight data analysis, aircraft performance models, Jeppesen flight planning system, or manufacturer specifications.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the arrival airport for this block time standard.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Direction of flight relative to the airline's hub or base. Outbound represents flights departing from hub; inbound represents flights arriving at hub. Block times may differ by direction due to prevailing winds and operational patterns.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this block time standard becomes effective and is used for schedule construction and crew pairing. Typically aligned with IATA season start dates.

attributes.name: etops_time_adjustment_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-Range Twin-Engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Time Adjustment (Minutes)
attributes.description: Additional block time in minutes for ETOPS-certified routes requiring extended-range twin-engine operations. Accounts for required routing to remain within diversion distance of suitable alternate airports.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA AC 120-42B

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this block time standard expires and is no longer used for schedule construction. Nullable for open-ended standards that remain effective until superseded.

attributes.name: fuel_planning_time_minutes
attributes.description: Block time used for fuel planning calculations, which may differ from scheduled block time to ensure adequate fuel reserves for contingencies, alternate airports, and regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: historical_average_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Historical average actual block time in minutes based on past flight performance data. Used for benchmarking and validating planned block time standards against operational reality.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this block time standard record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data governance requirements.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this block time standard was last reviewed and validated against actual flight performance data. Block time standards should be reviewed regularly (typically quarterly or seasonally) to ensure accuracy.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next review and validation of this block time standard. Ensures proactive maintenance of block time accuracy and alignment with operational performance.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing special considerations, operational constraints, seasonal factors, or other contextual information relevant to this block time standard. May include rationale for adjustments or known anomalies.

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the departure airport for this block time standard.

attributes.name: percentile_85_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: 85th percentile of historical actual block times in minutes. Represents the block time that 85% of flights achieve or beat. Used as a reliability target for schedule planning to balance OTP performance with schedule efficiency.

attributes.name: planned_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Total planned gate-to-gate block time in minutes, representing the scheduled duration from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks). This is the foundation for schedule construction, crew duty time calculations, and OTP measurement.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of historical flight records used to calculate this block time standard. Larger sample sizes provide greater statistical confidence in the standard's accuracy and reliability.

attributes.name: seasonal_adjustment_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this block time standard applies to summer season (typically March-October in Northern Hemisphere), winter season (typically October-March), or year-round. Seasonal variations account for prevailing winds, jet stream patterns, and daylight saving time impacts.

attributes.name: slot_constrained_adjustment_minutes
attributes.description: Additional time in minutes added to block time for slot-constrained airports where departure or arrival slot availability may require schedule padding to ensure slot compliance and reduce IROP risk.

attributes.name: standard_deviation_minutes
attributes.description: Standard deviation of historical block times in minutes, representing the variability and consistency of actual flight performance. Lower standard deviation indicates more predictable block times.

attributes.name: taxi_in_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned taxi-in time in minutes from landing (wheels-down) to gate arrival (on-blocks). Varies by airport layout, gate assignment, and ground traffic.

attributes.name: taxi_out_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned taxi-out time in minutes from gate departure (off-blocks) to takeoff (wheels-up). Varies by airport congestion, runway configuration, and time of day.

attributes.name: wind_adjustment_minutes
attributes.description: Adjustment in minutes to account for prevailing wind patterns, jet stream effects, and seasonal wind variations. Positive values indicate headwind penalties; negative values indicate tailwind benefits.
attributes.references: ICAO Meteorological Service for International Air Navigation

products.name: fleet_assignment
products.description: Transactional record of fleet type assignment to a route for a specific season or schedule period, capturing the planned aircraft type, sub-fleet variant, seat configuration, cabin class mix, gauge (total seats), cargo belly capacity, ETOPS requirement (for long-haul over-water routes), and assignment effective date range. Represents the planned fleet deployment decision linking network planning to fleet management. Aligns with Jeppesen NetLine/Fleet assignment module.
products.reference: Jeppesen NetLine/Fleet

attributes.name: fleet_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the route fleet assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft. Business justification: Fleet controllers assign specific tail numbers to route assignments for ETOPS compliance verification, maintenance routing, and operational control. fleet_assignment currently captures only aircraft_t

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Route fleet assignments must reference valid aircraft types for capacity planning, ETOPS compliance verification, seat configuration validation, and schedule feasibility analysis. Replaces denormalize

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Fleet assignments drive capacity and operating cost budgets — aircraft type selection determines fuel burn, crew costs, and maintenance reserves. Finance teams link fleet deployment plans to budget pl

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.cabin_configuration. Business justification: Revenue management and capacity planning require exact cabin configuration (seat counts by class) for each route assignment. fleet_assignment.seat_configuration_code is a denormalized text reference t

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Fleet assignments drive aircraft depreciation and lease cost allocation by route. Airlines allocate aircraft ownership costs (depreciation, lease payments, insurance) to route cost centres based on fl

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: Fleet assignments link specific leased aircraft to routes for lease cost allocation. Airlines track which lease contracts support which route assignments for IFRS 16 lease liability allocation, route

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route (origin-destination city pair) for which this fleet assignment is made.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA schedule season or planning period during which this fleet assignment is effective.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this fleet assignment was formally approved by network planning or fleet management authority.

attributes.name: approved_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the network planning manager or fleet planner who approved this fleet assignment.

attributes.name: assignment_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for this fleet assignment, used in operational planning and crew scheduling systems.

attributes.name: assignment_duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of days this fleet assignment is planned to be in effect, calculated from effective start to end date.

attributes.name: assignment_priority
attributes.description: Priority ranking of this fleet assignment relative to other assignments, used for conflict resolution and aircraft allocation decisions. Lower numbers indicate higher priority.

attributes.name: assignment_rationale
attributes.description: Business justification or reasoning for this specific fleet type assignment to the route, capturing strategic considerations such as demand patterns, competitive positioning, or operational constraints.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fleet assignment: planned (initial planning), confirmed (approved by network planning), active (in operation), suspended (temporarily paused), cancelled (assignment withdrawn), historical (past assignment for reference).

attributes.name: assignment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fleet assignment: permanent (year-round), seasonal (specific season only), temporary (short-term substitution), charter (ad-hoc charter operation), wet_lease (leased aircraft with crew), dry_lease (leased aircraft without crew).

attributes.name: business_class_seats
attributes.description: Number of business class seats in the assigned aircraft configuration.

attributes.name: cargo_belly_capacity_kg
attributes.description: Available cargo capacity in the belly hold of the assigned aircraft, measured in kilograms, used for cargo revenue planning.

attributes.name: cargo_belly_capacity_m3
attributes.description: Available cargo volume in the belly hold of the assigned aircraft, measured in cubic meters.

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fleet assignment is eligible for codeshare operations with partner airlines.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fleet assignment record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: days_of_operation
attributes.description: Days of the week this fleet assignment operates, represented as a string of digits 1-7 (1=Monday, 7=Sunday). Example: '1357' means Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Sunday.

attributes.name: economy_class_seats
attributes.description: Number of economy class seats in the assigned aircraft configuration.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this fleet assignment ends and the aircraft type is no longer assigned to this route. Null indicates an open-ended assignment.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this fleet assignment becomes effective and the assigned aircraft type begins operating the route.

attributes.name: etops_rating_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Rating (Minutes)
attributes.description: ETOPS rating in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330) indicating the maximum diversion time to an alternate airport that the aircraft and route are certified for.

attributes.name: etops_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether ETOPS certification is required for this route due to extended over-water or remote area operations.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6, FAA AC 120-42B, EASA Part-CAT

attributes.name: first_class_seats
attributes.description: Number of first class or premium cabin seats in the assigned aircraft configuration.

attributes.name: interline_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fleet assignment is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with other carriers.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fleet assignment record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing additional context, constraints, or special considerations for this fleet assignment.

attributes.name: planned_ask_capacity
attributes.description: Planned ASK (Available Seat Kilometers) capacity for this route-fleet assignment, calculated as total seats multiplied by route distance and frequency, used for network capacity planning.
attributes.references: IATA Industry Economics, Sabre AirVision Revenue Management

attributes.name: premium_economy_seats
attributes.description: Number of premium economy seats in the assigned aircraft configuration.

attributes.name: target_load_factor_percent
attributes.description: Target load factor percentage (percentage of seats filled) that revenue management aims to achieve for this route-fleet assignment.

attributes.name: total_seats
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats available on the assigned aircraft configuration, also known as gauge in airline revenue management.
attributes.references: Sabre AirVision Revenue Management, Jeppesen NetLine/Fleet

attributes.name: weekly_frequency
attributes.description: Number of flights per week planned for this route with the assigned fleet type during the assignment period.

products.name: carrier
products.description: Master reference table for carrier. Referenced by operating_carrier_id.

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Primary key for carrier

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Each carrier (airline) maps to a company code in the financial system for P&L reporting, intercompany eliminations, and regulatory filings. This is a foundational airline financial structure — carrier

attributes.name: parent_carrier_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on carrier (parent_carrier_id)

attributes.name: accounting_code
attributes.description: Three-digit numeric code assigned by IATA for financial settlement, ticketing, and interline accounting purposes.

attributes.name: alliance_membership
attributes.description: Global airline alliance to which the carrier belongs, enabling codeshare agreements, reciprocal benefits, and network coordination.

attributes.name: aoc_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier's Air Operator Certificate expires, if applicable.

attributes.name: aoc_issue_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier's current Air Operator Certificate was issued.

attributes.name: aoc_issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the civil aviation authority that issued the carrier's Air Operator Certificate.

attributes.name: aoc_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the carrier's Air Operator Certificate issued by the civil aviation authority.

attributes.name: callsign
attributes.description: Unique radio telephony callsign used by pilots and air traffic control for voice communications during flight operations.

attributes.name: cargo_operations_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier operates dedicated cargo or freight services.

attributes.name: carrier_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the airline carrier as registered with aviation authorities.

attributes.name: carrier_type
attributes.description: Classification of the carrier based on primary business model and service offering.

attributes.name: ceased_operations_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier permanently ceased flight operations, if applicable.

attributes.name: codeshare_participant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier participates in codeshare agreements with other carriers.

attributes.name: commenced_operations_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier began commercial flight operations.

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Primary contact email address for the carrier's corporate communications.

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for the carrier's customer service or corporate office.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country where the carrier is registered and holds its Air Operator Certificate (AOC).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this carrier record becomes effective for operational and scheduling purposes.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date until which this carrier record remains effective, nullable for open-ended records.

attributes.name: fleet_size
attributes.description: Total number of aircraft in the carrier's operational fleet.

attributes.name: founded_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier was originally established or incorporated.

attributes.name: headquarters_city
attributes.description: City where the carrier's corporate headquarters and primary administrative offices are located.

attributes.name: headquarters_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country where the carrier's headquarters is located.

attributes.name: hub_airport_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA airport codes representing the carrier's primary hub airports for network operations.

attributes.name: iata_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline designator code uniquely identifying the carrier in global distribution systems, reservations, and ticketing.

attributes.name: iata_member_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier is a member of the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

attributes.name: icao_code
attributes.description: Three-character ICAO airline designator code used in flight plans, air traffic control communications, and operational systems.

attributes.name: iosa_certification_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier received or last renewed its IOSA certification.

attributes.name: iosa_certified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier holds current IATA Operational Safety Audit (IOSA) certification.

attributes.name: iosa_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the carrier's current IOSA certification expires and requires renewal.

attributes.name: low_cost_carrier_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier operates under a low-cost carrier business model.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the carrier indicating whether it is actively operating flights.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this carrier record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this carrier record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: regional_carrier_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier primarily operates regional or short-haul routes.

attributes.name: trade_name
attributes.description: Commercial or marketing name under which the carrier operates and is known to passengers, may differ from legal name.

attributes.name: website_url
attributes.description: Primary website URL for the carrier's official online presence.

products.name: codeshare_agreement

attributes.name: renewed_codeshare_agreement_id

attributes.name: agreement_code

attributes.name: agreement_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the codeshare agreement for business reference and reporting.

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the codeshare agreement model defining inventory control and revenue sharing arrangements.

attributes.name: alliance_affiliation

attributes.name: auto_renewal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the codeshare agreement automatically renews upon expiration without explicit renegotiation.

attributes.name: baggage_allowance_harmonization

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference

attributes.name: block_space_seats
attributes.description: Number of seats allocated to the marketing carrier under block space codeshare arrangements.

attributes.name: codeshare_agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the codeshare agreement indicating operational validity and enforceability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this codeshare agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the codeshare agreement becomes binding and operational for flight inventory and revenue management.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the codeshare agreement terminates or requires renewal; nullable for evergreen agreements.

attributes.name: fare_basis_code_sharing_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether fare basis codes can be shared between operating and marketing carriers under this agreement.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_accrual_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers can earn frequent flyer miles on the marketing carriers program for codeshare flights.

attributes.name: interline_ticketing_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether interline ticketing is permitted under this codeshare agreement for multi-carrier itineraries.

attributes.name: inventory_control_party
attributes.description: Designates which carrier has authority over seat inventory management and availability control.

domains.name: safety
domains.description: Aviation safety management including SMS (Safety Management System), incident and occurrence reporting, accident investigation, CVR (Cockpit Voice Recorder) and FDR (Flight Data Recorder) event analysis, NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) tracking, hazard identification, risk assessment, safety audits, corrective action plans, SOP version control, and fatigue risk management. SSOT for all safety occurrence and risk data. Aligns with ICAO Annex 19 SMS framework.
domains.references: ICAO Annex 19, FAA SMS, EASA SMS

products.name: occurrence
products.description: Master record for all aviation safety occurrences including incidents, accidents, serious incidents, near-misses, and all occurrence subtypes (wildlife strikes, runway incursions, airspace deviations, dangerous goods incidents, CFIT events, loss of control, turbulence encounters) as defined under ICAO Annex 13 and Annex 19 SMS framework. Captures occurrence classification (accident/serious incident/incident/occurrence), ICAO occurrence category (CICTT taxonomy), occurrence subtype with subtype-specific extended attributes, date/time/location, aircraft registration, flight phase, injury severity, damage level, narrative description, initial causal factors, reporting source, and regulatory notification status. Subtype-specific fields accommodate wildlife strike details (species, aircraft part struck, ingestion), runway incursion details (runway designator, severity category A-D), airspace deviation details (cleared vs actual values), and dangerous goods details (UN number, DG class, packaging failure). SSOT for all safety occurrence data across the airline.
